1. # 🕵️ Intelligent Data Detective
2. 
3. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
4. [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
5. [![LangChain](https://img.shields.io/badge/LangChain-🦜🔗-green.svg)](https://python.langchain.com/)
6. [![LangGraph](https://img.shields.io/badge/LangGraph-🕸️-orange.svg)](https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/)
7. 
8. > **An intelligent multi-agent system that transforms raw data into actionable insights through automated data cleaning, exploratory analysis, visualization, and comprehensive reporting.**
9. 
10. ## 🎯 Overview
11. 
12. The Intelligent Data Detective is a sophisticated multi-agent system built with LangChain and LangGraph that revolutionizes the data analysis workflow. It combines the power of Large Language Models (LLMs) with specialized agents to perform comprehensive data analysis tasks autonomously.
13. 
14. ### 🚀 What It Does
15. 
16. - **🧹 Automated Data Cleaning**: Intelligently identifies and resolves data quality issues
17. - **📊 Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)**: Performs comprehensive statistical analysis and pattern discovery
18. - **🎨 Dynamic Visualization**: Creates relevant charts and graphs based on data insights
19. - **📝 Intelligent Reporting**: Generates structured, narrative reports with explanations
20. - **🤔 Chain-of-Thought Reasoning**: Provides transparent, step-by-step analytical reasoning
21. - **🌐 Contextual Web Search**: Enriches analysis with relevant external information
22. 
23. ### 💡 Key Innovation
24. 
25. Unlike traditional data analysis tools, the Intelligent Data Detective uses **collaborative AI agents** that work together, each specializing in different aspects of the data analysis pipeline. This approach ensures thorough, consistent, and explainable results.
26. 
27. ## 🏗️ Architecture
28. 
29. ### Multi-Agent System Design
30. 
31. ```mermaid
32. flowchart LR
33.     UI[🖥️ User Interface] --> Controller{🎯 Supervisor Agent}
34.     Controller --> Cleaner[🧹 Data Cleaner Agent]
35.     Controller --> Analyst[📊 Analyst Agent]
36.     Controller --> Viz[🎨 Visualization Agent]
37.     Controller --> Report[📝 Report Generator Agent]
38.     
39.     Cleaner -- Cleaned Data --> Analyst
40.     Analyst -- Insights --> Viz
41.     Viz -- Charts --> Report
42.     Report -- Final Report --> UI
43.     
44.     subgraph "🔄 Workflow Orchestration"
45.         Controller
46.     end
47.     
48.     subgraph "🛠️ Processing Agents"
49.         Cleaner
50.         Analyst
51.         Viz
52.         Report
53.     end
54. ```
55. 
56. ### 🤖 Agent Roles & Responsibilities
57. 
58. #### 🎯 **Supervisor Agent (Controller)**
59. - **Role**: Orchestrates the entire workflow and coordinates agent interactions
60. - **Responsibilities**: 
61.   - Manages task delegation and sequencing
62.   - Monitors agent completion status
63.   - Maintains global state and memory
64.   - Makes routing decisions based on current progress
65. 
66. #### 🧹 **Data Cleaner Agent**
67. - **Role**: Performs intelligent data preprocessing and quality assurance
68. - **Capabilities**:
69.   - Missing value detection and imputation strategies
70.   - Outlier identification and handling
71.   - Data type conversions and standardization
72.   - Duplicate detection and removal
73.   - Column name standardization
74. - **Tools**: pandas, numpy, custom data quality assessment tools
75. - **Output**: Cleaned dataset + detailed metadata about cleaning actions taken
76. 
77. #### 📊 **Analyst Agent**
78. - **Role**: Conducts comprehensive exploratory data analysis
79. - **Capabilities**:
80.   - Descriptive statistics computation
81.   - Correlation analysis and feature relationships
82.   - Anomaly and pattern detection
83.   - Hypothesis testing (normality, t-tests)
84.   - Basic machine learning model training
85.   - Data quality assessment
86. - **Tools**: pandas, scipy.stats, scikit-learn, custom analysis tools
87. - **Output**: Structured insights, correlations, anomalies, and visualization recommendations
88. 
89. #### 🎨 **Visualization Agent**
90. - **Role**: Creates compelling and relevant data visualizations
91. - **Capabilities**:
92.   - Histogram generation for distribution analysis
93.   - Scatter plots for relationship exploration
94.   - Correlation heatmaps for feature relationships
95.   - Box plots for outlier visualization
96.   - Dynamic chart selection based on data types and insights
97. - **Tools**: matplotlib, seaborn, base64 encoding for web compatibility
98. - **Output**: Generated visualizations with descriptive captions
99. 
100. #### 📝 **Report Generator Agent**
101. - **Role**: Synthesizes all findings into comprehensive, actionable reports
102. - **Capabilities**:
103.   - Multi-format report generation (HTML, Markdown, PDF)
104.   - Narrative synthesis from agent findings
105.   - Visual integration with explanatory text
106.   - Executive summary creation
107.   - Recommendation generation
108. - **Tools**: Jinja2 templating, xhtml2pdf, custom formatting tools
109. - **Output**: Professional reports combining text, statistics, and visualizations
110. 
111. ## ✨ Features
112. 
113. ### 🎯 **Core Features (Implemented)**
114. 
115. #### 🔄 **Automated Workflow Orchestration**
116. - Intelligent task routing between specialized agents
117. - State management with checkpointing and recovery
118. - Memory persistence across analysis sessions
119. - Real-time streaming updates during processing
120. 
121. #### 🧠 **Advanced Chain-of-Thought Reasoning**
122. - Transparent step-by-step analytical reasoning
123. - Decision logging for reproducibility
124. - Explainable AI approaches to data insights
125. - Audit trail for all analytical decisions
126.

128. - **Statistical Analysis**: Descriptive statistics, correlation matrices, hypothesis testing
129. - **Quality Assessment**: Missing value analysis, duplicate detection, data type validation
130. - **Pattern Recognition**: Anomaly detection, trend identification, relationship discovery
131. - **Machine Learning**: Basic classification and regression model training
132. 
133. #### 🎨 **Dynamic Visualization Generation**
134. - **Adaptive Chart Selection**: Automatically chooses appropriate visualization types
135. - **Interactive Elements**: Base64-encoded images for web integration
136. - **Custom Styling**: Configurable themes and color schemes
137. - **Multi-format Output**: PNG, SVG, and interactive plot support
138. 
139. #### 🌐 **Contextual Intelligence**
140. - **Web Search Integration**: Tavily API for external context and domain knowledge
141. - **Domain-Specific Insights**: Retrieval of relevant best practices and guidelines
142. - **Historical Learning**: Memory of past analysis patterns and decisions
143. 
144. #### 📊 **Flexible Data Handling**
145. - **Multiple Format Support**: CSV, JSON, Excel file processing
146. - **Large Dataset Optimization**: Efficient memory management and processing

173. - **Python 3.10+**: Primary programming language
174. - **LangChain**: LLM application framework and tool integration
175. - **LangGraph**: Multi-agent workflow orchestration

187. - **Jinja2**: Template engine for report generation
188. - **xhtml2pdf**: PDF report generation from HTML

191. - **Tavily API**: Web search and external context retrieval

197. - **Jupyter Notebooks**: Interactive development environment

202. ## 🚀 Quick Start
203. 
204. ### Prerequisites
205. 
206. - Python 3.10 or higher
207. - OpenAI API key
208. - Tavily API key (optional, for web search features)
209. 
210. ### Installation
211. 
212. 1. **Clone the repository**:
213.    ```bash
214.    git clone https://github.com/dhar174/intelligent_data_detective.git
215.    cd intelligent_data_detective
216.    ```
217. 
218. 2. **Set up environment variables**:
219.    ```bash
220.    export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-api-key"
221.    export TAVILY_API_KEY="your-tavily-api-key"  # Optional
222.    ```
223. 
224. 3. **Install dependencies**:
225.    ```bash
226.    pip install langchain langchain-core langchain-openai langchain_experimental langgraph
227.    pip install pandas numpy scipy scikit-learn matplotlib seaborn
228.    pip install pydantic python-dotenv tiktoken openpyxl xhtml2pdf
229.    pip install tavily-python chromadb joblib
230.    ```
231. 
232. ### 📊 Basic Usage
233. 
234. #### Using Jupyter Notebook (Recommended)
235. 
236. 1. **Open the main notebook**:
237.    ```bash
238.    jupyter notebook IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb
239.    ```
240. 
241. 2. **Configure your analysis**:
242.    ```python
243.    # Set your data source
244.    sample_prompt_text = "Analyze this customer review dataset for sentiment patterns and insights"
245.    
246.    # Configure analysis parameters
247.    config = {
248.        "configurable": {
249.            "thread_id": "data-analysis-session",
250.            "user_id": "analyst-1",
251.            "recursion_limit": 50
252.        }
253.    }
254.    ```
255. 
256. 3. **Run the analysis**:
257.    ```python
258.    # Execute the multi-agent workflow
259.    for chunk in data_detective_graph.stream(inputs, config=config, stream_mode="updates"):
260.        print(chunk)
261.    ```
262. 
263. #### Example Workflow
264. 
265. ```python
266. # Note: This project is currently notebook-based. Use the Jupyter notebook for analysis.
267. # Open IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb and run the cells
268. 
269. # Example of how to use the compiled graph from the notebook:
270. # After running the notebook setup cells (e.g., cells 1–5, which import libraries, initialize variables, and load data), you can use:
271. 
272. # Configure your analysis
273. inputs = {
274.     "user_prompt": "Identify key patterns and anomalies in this sales data",
275.     "df_ids": ["sales_data_2023"],  # Replace "sales_data_2023" with the actual dataframe ID obtained from the notebook setup cells
276.     "messages": []
277. }
278. 
279. config = {
280.     "configurable": {
281.         "thread_id": "data-analysis-session",
282.         "user_id": "analyst-1"
283.     },
284.     "recursion_limit": 50
285. }
286. 
287. # Run the analysis using the compiled graph
288. for chunk in data_detective_graph.stream(inputs, config=config, stream_mode="updates"):
289.     print(chunk)
290. ```

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """
3. Unit tests for Intelligent Data Detective components.
4. 
5. This file tests the key components from the IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb notebook
6. to ensure they work correctly and catch any bugs.
7. """
8. 
9. import unittest
10. import tempfile
11. import pandas as pd
12. import numpy as np
13. import json
14. import uuid
15. from pathlib import Path
16. from collections import OrderedDict
17. from typing import Dict, Optional, List, Tuple, Union
18. from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError, model_validator
19. 
20. # Test the Pydantic models
21. class AnalysisConfig(BaseModel):
22.     """User-configurable settings for the data analysis workflow."""
23.     default_visualization_style: str = Field("seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid", description="Default style for matplotlib/seaborn visualizations.")
24.     report_author: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Author name to include in generated reports.")
25.     datetime_format_preference: str = Field("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", description="Preferred format for datetime string representations.")
26.     large_dataframe_preview_rows: int = Field(5, description="Number of rows for previewing large dataframes.")
27. 
28. class CleaningMetadata(BaseModel):
29.     """Metadata about the data cleaning actions taken."""
30.     steps_taken: list[str] = Field(description="List of cleaning steps performed.")
31.     data_description_after_cleaning: str = Field(description="Brief description of the dataset after cleaning.")
32. 
33. class InitialDescription(BaseModel):
34.     """Initial description of the dataset."""
35.     dataset_description: str = Field(description="Brief description of the dataset.")
36.     data_sample: Optional[str] = Field(description="Sample of the data (first few rows).")
37. 
38. class AnalysisInsights(BaseModel):
39.     """Insights from the exploratory data analysis."""
40.     summary: str = Field(description="Overall summary of EDA findings.")
41.     correlation_insights: str = Field(description="Key correlation insights identified.")
42.     anomaly_insights: str = Field(description="Anomalies or interesting patterns detected.")
43.     recommended_visualizations: list[str] = Field(description="List of recommended visualizations to illustrate findings.")
44.     recommended_next_steps: Optional[List[str]] = Field(None, description="List of recommended next analysis steps or questions to investigate based on the findings.")
45. 
46. class CellIdentifier(BaseModel):
47.     """Identifies a single cell by row index and column name."""
48.     row_index: int = Field(..., description="Row index of the cell.")
49.     column_name: str = Field(..., description="Column name of the cell.")
50. 
51. class GetDataParams(BaseModel):
52.     """Parameters for retrieving data from the DataFrame."""
53.     df_id: str = Field(..., description="DataFrame ID in the global registry.")
54.     index: Union[int, List[int], Tuple[int, int]] = Field(..., description="Specifies the rows to retrieve. Can be: 1) A single integer for one row. 2) A list of integers for multiple specific rows. 3) A 2-element tuple (start, end) for a range of rows (inclusive).")
55.     columns: Union[str, List[str]] = Field("all", description="A string (single column), a list of strings (multiple columns), or 'all' for all columns (default: 'all').")
56.     cells: Optional[List[CellIdentifier]] = Field(None, description="A list of cell identifier objects, each specifying a 'row_index' and 'column_name'.")
57. 
58.     @model_validator(mode='before')
59.     def validate_index(cls, values):
60.         index = values.get('index')
61.         if not isinstance(index, (int, list, tuple)):
62.             raise ValueError("Invalid 'index' type. Must be int, list, or tuple.")
63.         if isinstance(index, tuple) and len(index) != 2:
64.             raise ValueError("Invalid tuple length for 'index'. Must be a 2-tuple for range.")
65.         if isinstance(index, list) and not all(isinstance(i, int) for i in index):
66.             raise ValueError("Invalid list elements for 'index'. Must contain only integers.")
67.         return values
68. 
69. class DataFrameRegistry:
70.     """Simplified DataFrameRegistry for testing."""
71.     def __init__(self, capacity=20):
72.         self.registry: Dict[str, dict] = {}
73.         self.df_id_to_raw_path: Dict[str, str] = {}
74.         self.cache = OrderedDict()
75.         self.capacity = capacity
76. 
77.     def register_dataframe(self, df=None, df_id=None, raw_path=""):
78.         if df_id is None:
79.             df_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
80.         if raw_path == "":
81.             raw_path = f"/tmp/{df_id}.csv"
82.         self.registry[df_id] = {"df": df, "raw_path": str(raw_path)}
83.         self.df_id_to_raw_path[df_id] = str(raw_path)
84.         if df is not None:
85.             self.cache[df_id] = df
86.             if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
87.                 self.cache.popitem(last=False)
88.         return df_id
89. 
90.     def get_dataframe(self, df_id: str, load_if_not_exists=False):
91.         if df_id in self.cache:
92.             self.cache.move_to_end(df_id)
93.             return self.cache[df_id]
94.         
95.         if df_id in self.registry:
96.             df_data = self.registry[df_id]
97.             df = df_data.get("df")
98.             if df is not None:
99.                 self.cache[df_id] = df
100.                 if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
101.                     self.cache.popitem(last=False)
102.                 return df
103.             elif load_if_not_exists and df_data.get("raw_path"):
104.                 try:
105.                     loaded_df = pd.read_csv(df_data["raw_path"])
106.                     self.registry[df_id]["df"] = loaded_df
107.                     self.cache[df_id] = loaded_df
108.                     if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
109.                         self.cache.popitem(last=False)
110.                     return loaded_df
111.                 except FileNotFoundError:
112.                     return None
113.                 except Exception as e:
114.                     print(f"Error loading DataFrame from {df_data['raw_path']}: {e}")
115.                     return None
116.         return None
117. 
118.     def remove_dataframe(self, df_id: str):
119.         if df_id in self.registry:
120.             del self.registry[df_id]
121.             if df_id in self.cache:
122.                 del self.cache[df_id]
123.             del self.df_id_to_raw_path[df_id]
124.             
125.     def get_raw_path_from_id(self, df_id: str):
126.         return self.df_id_to_raw_path.get(df_id)

300. class TestToolFunctions(unittest.TestCase):
301.     """Test individual tool functions that can be extracted from the notebook."""
302.     
303.     def setUp(self):
304.         """Set up test fixtures."""
305.         self.registry = DataFrameRegistry()
306.         self.test_df = pd.DataFrame({

308.             'string_col': ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'],

310.         })
311.         self.df_id = self.registry.register_dataframe(self.test_df, "test_df")

313.     def test_get_column_names_functionality(self):

319.         actual_columns = df.columns.tolist()

322.     def test_check_missing_values_functionality(self):
323.         """Test the logic behind check_missing_values tool."""

325.         missing_values = df.isnull().sum()
326.         
327.         # Should have 1 missing value in numeric_col and 1 in mixed_col
328.         self.assertEqual(missing_values['numeric_col'], 1)
329.         self.assertEqual(missing_values['string_col'], 0)

332.     def test_drop_column_functionality(self):
333.         """Test the logic behind drop_column tool."""

335.         original_columns = df.columns.tolist()
336.

339.         expected_columns = ['numeric_col', 'mixed_col']
340.         self.assertEqual(df_modified.columns.tolist(), expected_columns)
341.         
342.         # Original df should be unchanged (since we didn't use inplace=True)
343.         self.assertEqual(df.columns.tolist(), original_columns)
344.     
345.     def test_fill_missing_median_functionality(self):
346.         """Test the logic behind fill_missing_median tool."""
347.         df = self.registry.get_dataframe(self.df_id).copy()
348.         
349.         # Calculate median of numeric_col (excluding NaN)
350.         median_value = df['numeric_col'].median()  # Should be 2.5
351.         self.assertEqual(median_value, 2.5)
352.         
353.         # Fill missing values
354.         df.fillna({'numeric_col': median_value}, inplace=True)
355.         
356.         # Should have no missing values now
357.         self.assertEqual(df['numeric_col'].isnull().sum(), 0)
358.         # Value at index 3 should be the median
359.         self.assertEqual(df.loc[3, 'numeric_col'], median_value)

421.     def test_parentheses_balance_in_description(self):
422.         """Test that description strings have balanced parentheses."""
423.         # This tests the bug fix for unbalanced parentheses in field descriptions
424.         # The original had `(start, end)` which created extra unmatched parentheses
425.         description = "Specifies the rows to retrieve. Can be: 1) A single integer for one row. 2) A list of integers for multiple specific rows. 3) A 2-element tuple (start, end) for a range of rows (inclusive)."
426.         
427.         open_count = description.count('(')
428.         close_count = description.count(')')
429.         
430.         # The numbered items 1), 2), 3) contribute 3 close parentheses
431.         # (start, end) contributes 1 open and 1 close
432.         # (inclusive) contributes 1 open and 1 close
433.         # Total: 2 open, 5 close - this is actually the fixed state
434.         
435.         # Let's test a simpler case that should be balanced
436.         simple_description = "A tuple with start and end values for range selection."
437.         simple_open = simple_description.count('(')
438.         simple_close = simple_description.count(')')
439.         self.assertEqual(simple_open, simple_close, "Simple descriptions should have balanced parentheses")

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """
3. Enhanced Memory System for Intelligent Data Detective
4. 
5. This module provides structured multi-namespace categorization for memory types,
6. enabling targeted memory retrieval for different agent roles (analysis, cleaning, 
7. visualization) and preventing noise in memory search results.
8. 
9. Key Features:
10. - Hierarchical memory namespaces by category
11. - Filtered retrieval with graceful fallback
12. - Backward compatibility with existing generic namespace
13. - Configurable limits per memory kind
14. - Memory lifecycle management with TTL, pruning, and importance scoring
15. - Policy-driven retention and relevance weighting
16. """
17. 
18. import time
19. import uuid
20. import math
21. import logging
22. import yaml
23. import os
24. from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union, Literal, Any
25. from dataclasses import dataclass, field
26. from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore
27. from langchain_core.runnables.config import RunnableConfig
28. from langchain_core.messages import BaseMessage
29. from langgraph.graph import MessagesState
30. 
31. # Type definitions for memory kinds
32. MemoryKind = Literal["conversation", "analysis", "cleaning", "visualization", "insights", "errors"]
33. 
34. # Memory record schema with lifecycle management
35. @dataclass
36. class MemoryRecord:
37.     """Enhanced memory record with lifecycle management fields."""
38.     id: str
39.     kind: str
40.     text: str
41.     vector: Optional[List[float]] = None
42.     created_at: float = field(default_factory=time.time)

1. # Diagram Recipes
2. 
3. Use these recipes to choose the right diagram and keep the output explainable.
4. 
5. ## Pick the Right Artifact
6. 
7. | User ask | Best output | Notes |
8. | --- | --- | --- |
9. | "Show me the architecture" | Mermaid + `package` granularity | Start broad, then zoom in |
10. | "Which modules import which?" | Mermaid or DOT + `module` granularity | Narrow to one subsystem when possible |
11. | "Which files depend on which env vars?" | Mermaid + `env` + `file` granularity | Good for config audits |
12. | "Give me something I can polish in Figma" | Mermaid + `figma-json` | Treat Mermaid as source of truth |
13. | "Turn the docs into a visual map" | `$markmap-cli` | Better for Markdown than code edges |
14. 
15. ## Output Conventions
16. 
17. - Default generated diagrams to `docs/diagrams/` when the repo already has a docs folder.
18. - Use descriptive names such as `repo-package-map`, `generator-map`, or `env-map`.
19. - Keep the generated source file even if you later render SVG or draw the same view in Figma.
20. 
21. ## Command Recipes
22. 
23. ### High-level repo map
24. 
25. ```bash
26. python scripts/generate_repo_diagram.py \
27.   --repo . \
28.   --scan-root src \
29.   --kind imports \
30.   --granularity package \
31.   --package-depth 2 \
32.   --emit mermaid,dot,json \
33.   --name repo-package-map \
34.   --output-dir docs/diagrams
35. ```
36. 
37. ### Focused subsystem map
38. 
39. ```bash
40. python scripts/generate_repo_diagram.py \
41.   --repo . \
42.   --scan-root src/langgraph_system_generator/generator \
43.   --kind mixed \
44.   --granularity module \
45.   --emit mermaid,dot,figma-json \
46.   --name generator-map \
47.   --output-dir docs/diagrams
48. ```
49. 
50. ### Config usage map
51. 
52. ```bash
53. python scripts/generate_repo_diagram.py \
54.   --repo . \
55.   --scan-root src \
56.   --kind env \
57.   --granularity file \
58.   --emit mermaid,json \
59.   --name env-map \
60.   --output-dir docs/diagrams
61. ```
62. 
63. ### DOT plus SVG
64. 
65. ```bash
66. python scripts/generate_repo_diagram.py \
67.   --repo . \
68.   --scan-root src \
69.   --kind imports \
70.   --granularity package \
71.   --emit dot \
72.   --render-svg \
73.   --name repo-package-map \
74.   --output-dir docs/diagrams
75. ```
76. 
77. ## Figma Transfer Recipe
78. 
79. 1. Generate a `*.figma.json` file.
80. 2. Create a new design file with `$figma-create-new-file`.
81. 3. Load `$figma-use`.
82. 4. Create one frame per `group`.
83. 5. Create one rectangle per node using the provided `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`.
84. 6. Add labels directly from the `label` field.
85. 7. Draw lines for each edge. Use solid lines for `imports` and dashed lines for `reads-env`.
86. 
87. ## Keep the Diagram Useful
88. 
89. - Prefer multiple focused diagrams over one giant repo graph.
90. - If one top-level package dominates the whole repo, increase `--package-depth`.
91. - When a repo already contains a decorative visualization such as a packed SVG, use it only as orientation. Generate Mermaid or DOT for explainable maintenance work.
92.

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """Generate Mermaid, DOT, JSON, and Figma-ready repo diagrams from Python code."""
3. 
4. from __future__ import annotations
5. 
6. import argparse
7. import ast
8. import json
9. import re
10. import shutil
11. import subprocess
12. from collections import defaultdict
13. from dataclasses import dataclass
14. from pathlib import Path
15. from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple
16. 
17. EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES = {
18.     ".git",
19.     ".hg",
20.     ".mypy_cache",
21.     ".next",
22.     ".pytest_cache",
23.     ".ruff_cache",
24.     ".svn",
25.     ".tox",
26.     ".venv",
27.     "__pycache__",
28.     "build",
29.     "dist",
30.     "node_modules",
31.     "site-packages",
32.     "venv",
33. }
34. 
35. ENV_PATTERNS = [
36.     re.compile(r"""os\.getenv\(\s*['"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)['"]"""),
37.     re.compile(r"""os\.environ\.get\(\s*['"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)['"]"""),
38.     re.compile(r"""os\.environ\[\s*['"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)['"]\s*\]"""),
39.     re.compile(r"""getenv\(\s*['"]([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)['"]"""),
40. ]
41. 
42. 
43. @dataclass(frozen=True)
44. class ModuleRecord:
45.     module: str
46.     relpath: str
47.     text: str
48.     tree: ast.AST
49. 
50. 
51. @dataclass(frozen=True)
52. class Edge:
53.     source: str
54.     target: str
55.     kind: str
56. 
57. 
58. @dataclass(frozen=True)
59. class DiagramNode:
60.     node_id: str
61.     label: str
62.     node_type: str
63.     group: str
64. 
65. 
66. def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
67.     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
68.         description="Generate repository diagrams from Python imports and environment variable usage."
69.     )
70.     parser.add_argument("--repo", default=".", help="Repository root to scan")
71.     parser.add_argument(
72.         "--scan-root",
73.         action="append",
74.         default=[],
75.         help="Relative path under the repo to scan. Repeatable. Defaults to src when present, else repo root.",
76.     )
77.     parser.add_argument(
78.         "--kind",
79.         choices=["imports", "env", "mixed"],
80.         default="mixed",
81.         help="Relationship family to diagram",
82.     )
83.     parser.add_argument(
84.         "--granularity",
85.         choices=["package", "module", "file"],
86.         default="package",
87.         help="Node granularity",
88.     )
89.     parser.add_argument(
90.         "--package-depth",
91.         type=int,
92.         default=2,
93.         help="Package prefix depth when granularity=package",
94.     )
95.     parser.add_argument(
96.         "--group-depth",
97.         type=int,
98.         default=2,
99.         help="Package depth used for subgraph grouping",
100.     )
101.     parser.add_argument(
102.         "--emit",
103.         default="mermaid,dot,json",
104.         help="Comma-separated output formats: mermaid,dot,json,figma-json",
105.     )
106.     parser.add_argument("--name", default="repo-diagram", help="Base output file name")
107.     parser.add_argument(
108.         "--output-dir",
109.         default="repo-diagrams",
110.         help="Directory for generated artifacts",
111.     )
112.     parser.add_argument(
113.         "--exclude",
114.         action="append",
115.         default=[],
116.         help="Glob-like relative path excludes. Repeatable.",
117.     )
118.     parser.add_argument(
119.         "--render-svg",
120.         action="store_true",
121.         help="Render an SVG from the DOT file when Graphviz is installed",
122.     )
123.     return parser.parse_args()
124. 
125. 
126. def choose_scan_roots(repo_root: Path, requested_roots: Sequence[str]) -> List[Path]:
127.     if requested_roots:
128.         roots = [repo_root / root for root in requested_roots]
129.     elif (repo_root / "src").exists():
130.         roots = [repo_root / "src"]
131.     else:
132.         roots = [repo_root]
133.     return [root.resolve() for root in roots if root.exists()]
134. 
135. 
136. def is_excluded(path: Path, repo_root: Path, extra_excludes: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
137.     if any(part in EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES for part in path.parts):
138.         return True
139.     relpath = path.resolve().relative_to(repo_root.resolve()).as_posix()
140.     return any(Path(relpath).match(pattern) for pattern in extra_excludes)
141. 
142. 
143. def module_name_from_path(scan_root: Path, file_path: Path) -> str:
144.     rel = file_path.relative_to(scan_root)
145.     parts = list(rel.parts)
146.     if parts[-1] == "__init__.py":
147.         parts = parts[:-1]
148.     else:
149.         parts[-1] = parts[-1][:-3]
150.     return ".".join(part for part in parts if part)
151. 
152. 
153. def collect_modules(
154.     repo_root: Path, scan_roots: Sequence[Path], extra_excludes: Sequence[str]
155. ) -> Dict[str, ModuleRecord]:
156.     modules: Dict[str, ModuleRecord] = {}
157.     for scan_root in scan_roots:
158.         for file_path in scan_root.rglob("*.py"):
159.             if is_excluded(file_path, repo_root, extra_excludes):
160.                 continue
161.             module_name = module_name_from_path(scan_root, file_path)
162.             if not module_name:
163.                 continue
164.             text = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
165.             try:
166.                 tree = ast.parse(text, filename=str(file_path))
167.             except SyntaxError:
168.                 continue
169.             relpath = file_path.resolve().relative_to(repo_root.resolve()).as_posix()
170.             modules[module_name] = ModuleRecord(
171.                 module=module_name,
172.                 relpath=relpath,
173.                 text=text,
174.                 tree=tree,
175.             )
176.     return modules
177. 
178. 
179. def best_internal_target(candidate: str, module_names: Set[str]) -> Optional[str]:
180.     parts = candidate.split(".")
181.     for length in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
182.         probe = ".".join(parts[:length])
183.         if probe in module_names:
184.             return probe
185.     return None
186. 
187. 
188. def resolve_relative_import(current_module: str, level: int, imported_module: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
189.     package_parts = current_module.split(".")[:-1]
190.     if level > len(package_parts) + 1:
191.         return None
192.     if level > 0:
193.         package_parts = package_parts[: len(package_parts) - (level - 1)]
194.     if imported_module:
195.         package_parts.extend(imported_module.split("."))
196.     return ".".join(part for part in package_parts if part)
197. 
198. 
199. def extract_import_edges(modules: Dict[str, ModuleRecord]) -> Set[Edge]:
200.     module_names = set(modules.keys())
201.     edges: Set[Edge] = set()
202. 
203.     for record in modules.values():
204.         for node in ast.walk(record.tree):
205.             if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
206.                 for alias in node.names:
207.                     target = best_internal_target(alias.name, module_names)
208.                     if target and target != record.module:
209.                         edges.add(Edge(record.module, target, "imports"))
210. 
211.             if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
212.                 base = resolve_relative_import(record.module, node.level, node.module)
213.                 candidates: List[str] = []
214.                 if base:
215.                     for alias in node.names:
216.                         if alias.name == "*":
217.                             continue
218.                         candidates.append(f"{base}.{alias.name}")
219.                     candidates.append(base)
220.                 for candidate in candidates:
221.                     target = best_internal_target(candidate, module_names)
222.                     if target and target != record.module:
223.                         edges.add(Edge(record.module, target, "imports"))
224.                         break
225. 
226.     return edges
227. 
228. 
229. def extract_env_edges(modules: Dict[str, ModuleRecord]) -> Set[Edge]:
230.     edges: Set[Edge] = set()
231.     for record in modules.values():
232.         env_vars: Set[str] = set()
233.         for pattern in ENV_PATTERNS:
234.             env_vars.update(pattern.findall(record.text))
235.         for env_var in sorted(env_vars):
236.             edges.add(Edge(record.module, env_var, "reads-env"))
237.     return edges
238. 
239. 
240. def collapse_node_id(
241.     raw_id: str,
242.     modules: Dict[str, ModuleRecord],
243.     granularity: str,
244.     package_depth: int,
245.     group_depth: int,
246. ) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
247.     if raw_id not in modules:
248.         return raw_id, raw_id, "environment"
249. 
250.     record = modules[raw_id]
251. 
252.     if granularity == "file":
253.         label = record.relpath
254.         parent_parts = record.relpath.split("/")[:-1]
255.         group = "/".join(parent_parts[: max(1, min(len(parent_parts), group_depth))]) if parent_parts else "."
256.         return label, label, group
257. 
258.     if granularity == "module":
259.         parts = record.module.split(".")
260.         group = ".".join(parts[: max(1, min(len(parts) - 1, group_depth))]) if len(parts) > 1 else parts[0]
261.         return record.module, record.module, group
262. 
263.     parts = record.module.split(".")
264.     collapsed = ".".join(parts[: min(package_depth, len(parts))])
265.     group = parts[0]
266.     return collapsed, collapsed, group
267. 
268. 
269. def build_diagram(
270.     modules: Dict[str, ModuleRecord],
271.     raw_edges: Iterable[Edge],
272.     granularity: str,
273.     package_depth: int,
274.     group_depth: int,
275. ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, DiagramNode], List[Edge]]:
276.     nodes: Dict[str, DiagramNode] = {}
277.     edges: Set[Edge] = set()
278. 
279.     for edge in raw_edges:
280.         source_id, source_label, source_group = collapse_node_id(
281.             edge.source, modules, granularity, package_depth, group_depth
282.         )
283.         target_id, target_label, target_group = collapse_node_id(
284.             edge.target, modules, granularity, package_depth, group_depth
285.         )
286. 
287.         nodes[source_id] = DiagramNode(source_id, source_label, "code", source_group)
288.         target_type = "environment" if edge.kind == "reads-env" else "code"
289.         nodes[target_id] = DiagramNode(target_id, target_label, target_type, target_group)
290. 
291.         if source_id != target_id:
292.             edges.add(Edge(source_id, target_id, edge.kind))
293. 
294.     return nodes, sorted(edges, key=lambda item: (item.source, item.target, item.kind))
295. 
296. 
297. def sanitize_mermaid_id(value: str) -> str:
298.     sanitized = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", value)
299.     if not sanitized or sanitized[0].isdigit():
300.         sanitized = f"n_{sanitized}"
301.     return sanitized
302. 
303. 
304. def make_mermaid(nodes: Dict[str, DiagramNode], edges: Sequence[Edge], title: str) -> str:
305.     node_ids = {node_id: sanitize_mermaid_id(node_id) for node_id in nodes}
306.     groups: Dict[str, List[DiagramNode]] = defaultdict(list)
307.     for node in nodes.values():
308.         groups[node.group].append(node)
309. 
310.     lines = [
311.         "flowchart LR",
312.         f"%% {title}",
313.     ]
314. 
315.     for group_name in sorted(groups):
316.         group_nodes = sorted(groups[group_name], key=lambda item: item.label)
317.         if group_name != "environment" and len(group_nodes) > 1:
318.             lines.append(f'    subgraph {sanitize_mermaid_id(group_name)}["{group_name}"]')
319.             for node in group_nodes:
320.                 node_id = node_ids[node.node_id]
321.                 if node.node_type == "environment":
322.                     lines.append(f'        {node_id}(["{node.label}"])')
323.                 else:
324.                     lines.append(f'        {node_id}["{node.label}"]')
325.             lines.append("    end")
326.         else:
327.             for node in group_nodes:
328.                 node_id = node_ids[node.node_id]
329.                 if node.node_type == "environment":
330.                     lines.append(f'    {node_id}(["{node.label}"])')
331.                 else:
332.                     lines.append(f'    {node_id}["{node.label}"]')
333. 
334.     lines.append("")
335.     for edge in edges:
336.         source_id = node_ids[edge.source]
337.         target_id = node_ids[edge.target]
338.         if edge.kind == "imports":
339.             lines.append(f"    {source_id} --> {target_id}")
340.         else:
341.             lines.append(f"    {source_id} -. reads .-> {target_id}")
342. 
343.     lines.extend(
344.         [
345.             "",
346.             "    classDef code fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#3730a3,stroke-width:1.5px",
347.             "    classDef environment fill:#fff7ed,stroke:#c2410c,stroke-width:1.5px",
348.         ]
349.     )
350. 
351.     for node in sorted(nodes.values(), key=lambda item: item.label):
352.         class_name = "environment" if node.node_type == "environment" else "code"
353.         lines.append(f"    class {node_ids[node.node_id]} {class_name}")
354. 
355.     return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
356. 
357. 
358. def make_dot(nodes: Dict[str, DiagramNode], edges: Sequence[Edge], title: str) -> str:
359.     def quote(value: str) -> str:
360.         return json.dumps(value)
361. 
362.     groups: Dict[str, List[DiagramNode]] = defaultdict(list)
363.     for node in nodes.values():
364.         groups[node.group].append(node)
365. 
366.     lines = [
367.         "digraph repo_diagram {",
368.         f"  label={quote(title)};",
369.         "  labelloc=t;",
370.         '  graph [rankdir=LR, fontsize=18, fontname="Arial"];',
371.         '  node [shape=box, style="rounded,filled", fontname="Arial", fillcolor="#EEF2FF", color="#3730A3"];',
372.         '  edge [fontname="Arial", color="#6B7280"];',
373.     ]
374. 
375.     cluster_index = 0
376.     for group_name in sorted(groups):
377.         group_nodes = sorted(groups[group_name], key=lambda item: item.label)
378.         if group_name != "environment" and len(group_nodes) > 1:
379.             lines.append(f"  subgraph cluster_{cluster_index} {{")
380.             lines.append(f"    label={quote(group_name)};")
381.             lines.append('    color="#CBD5E1";')
382.             for node in group_nodes:
383.                 lines.append(f"    {quote(node.node_id)} [label={quote(node.label)}];")
384.             lines.append("  }")
385.             cluster_index += 1
386.         else:
387.             for node in group_nodes:
388.                 if node.node_type == "environment":
389.                     lines.append(
390.                         f'  {quote(node.node_id)} [label={quote(node.label)}, shape=hexagon, fillcolor="#FFF7ED", color="#C2410C"];'
391.                     )
392.                 else:
393.                     lines.append(f"  {quote(node.node_id)} [label={quote(node.label)}];")
394. 
395.     for edge in edges:
396.         if edge.kind == "imports":
397.             lines.append(f"  {quote(edge.source)} -> {quote(edge.target)};")
398.         else:
399.             lines.append(
400.                 f'  {quote(edge.source)} -> {quote(edge.target)} [style=dashed, color="#C2410C", label="reads"];'
401.             )
402. 
403.     lines.append("}")
404.     return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
405. 
406. 
407. def make_json_payload(
408.     nodes: Dict[str, DiagramNode], edges: Sequence[Edge], args: argparse.Namespace, repo_root: Path
409. ) -> str:
410.     payload = {
411.         "repo": str(repo_root),
412.         "kind": args.kind,
413.         "granularity": args.granularity,
414.         "package_depth": args.package_depth,
415.         "nodes": [
416.             {
417.                 "id": node.node_id,
418.                 "label": node.label,
419.                 "type": node.node_type,
420.                 "group": node.group,
421.             }
422.             for node in sorted(nodes.values(), key=lambda item: (item.group, item.label))
423.         ],
424.         "edges": [
425.             {"source": edge.source, "target": edge.target, "kind": edge.kind}
426.             for edge in edges
427.         ],
428.     }
429.     return json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n"
430. 
431. 
432. def make_figma_payload(
433.     nodes: Dict[str, DiagramNode], edges: Sequence[Edge], args: argparse.Namespace, repo_root: Path
434. ) -> str:
435.     groups: Dict[str, List[DiagramNode]] = defaultdict(list)
436.     for node in nodes.values():
437.         groups[node.group].append(node)
438. 
439.     ordered_groups = sorted(groups.keys(), key=lambda item: (item == "environment", item))
440.     layout_nodes = []
441.     for column_index, group_name in enumerate(ordered_groups):
442.         for row_index, node in enumerate(sorted(groups[group_name], key=lambda item: item.label)):
443.             width = 240 if node.node_type == "code" else 200
444.             height = 72 if node.node_type == "code" else 56
445.             layout_nodes.append(
446.                 {
447.                     "id": node.node_id,
448.                     "label": node.label,
449.                     "type": node.node_type,
450.                     "group": node.group,
451.                     "x": column_index * 340,
452.                     "y": row_index * 120,
453.                     "width": width,
454.                     "height": height,
455.                 }
456.             )
457. 
458.     payload = {
459.         "repo": str(repo_root),
460.         "kind": args.kind,
461.         "granularity": args.granularity,
462.         "nodes": layout_nodes,
463.         "edges": [
464.             {"source": edge.source, "target": edge.target, "kind": edge.kind}
465.             for edge in edges
466.         ],
467.         "legend": {
468.             "code": {"fill": "#EEF2FF", "stroke": "#3730A3"},
469.             "environment": {"fill": "#FFF7ED", "stroke": "#C2410C"},
470.             "imports": {"line_style": "solid"},
471.             "reads-env": {"line_style": "dashed"},
472.         },
473.     }
474.     return json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n"
475. 
476. 
477. def write_output(output_path: Path, contents: str) -> None:
478.     output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
479.     output_path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
480. 
481. 
482. def maybe_render_svg(dot_path: Path) -> Optional[Path]:
483.     dot_binary = shutil.which("dot")
484.     if not dot_binary:
485.         raise SystemExit("Graphviz 'dot' was not found on PATH. Install Graphviz or omit --render-svg.")
486.     svg_path = dot_path.with_suffix(".svg")
487.     subprocess.run([dot_binary, "-Tsvg", str(dot_path), "-o", str(svg_path)], check=True)
488.     return svg_path
489. 
490. 
491. def main() -> int:
492.     args = parse_args()
493.     repo_root = Path(args.repo).resolve()
494.     output_dir = (repo_root / args.output_dir).resolve()
495.     scan_roots = choose_scan_roots(repo_root, args.scan_root)
496.     emit_formats = [item.strip() for item in args.emit.split(",") if item.strip()]
497. 
498.     if not scan_roots:
499.         raise SystemExit("No scan roots were found.")
500. 
501.     modules = collect_modules(repo_root, scan_roots, args.exclude)
502.     if not modules:
503.         raise SystemExit("No Python modules were found in the requested scan roots.")
504. 
505.     raw_edges: Set[Edge] = set()
506.     if args.kind in {"imports", "mixed"}:
507.         raw_edges.update(extract_import_edges(modules))
508.     if args.kind in {"env", "mixed"}:
509.         raw_edges.update(extract_env_edges(modules))
510. 
511.     if not raw_edges:
512.         raise SystemExit("No matching relationships were found for the requested diagram kind.")
513. 
514.     nodes, edges = build_diagram(
515.         modules,
516.         raw_edges,
517.         args.granularity,
518.         args.package_depth,
519.         args.group_depth,
520.     )
521.     title = f"{repo_root.name}: {args.kind} {args.granularity} diagram"
522. 
523.     writers = {
524.         "mermaid": (".mmd", make_mermaid(nodes, edges, title)),
525.         "dot": (".dot", make_dot(nodes, edges, title)),
526.         "json": (".json", make_json_payload(nodes, edges, args, repo_root)),
527.         "figma-json": (".figma.json", make_figma_payload(nodes, edges, args, repo_root)),
528.     }
529. 
530.     written_paths: List[Path] = []
531.     for output_format in emit_formats:
532.         if output_format not in writers:
533.             raise SystemExit(f"Unsupported output format: {output_format}")
534.         suffix, contents = writers[output_format]
535.         output_path = output_dir / f"{args.name}{suffix}"
536.         write_output(output_path, contents)
537.         written_paths.append(output_path)
538. 
539.     if args.render_svg:
540.         dot_candidates = [path for path in written_paths if path.suffix == ".dot"]
541.         if not dot_candidates:
542.             raise SystemExit("--render-svg requires dot output. Include 'dot' in --emit.")
543.         svg_path = maybe_render_svg(dot_candidates[0])
544.         if svg_path:
545.             written_paths.append(svg_path)
546. 
547.     summary = {
548.         "repo": str(repo_root),
549.         "scan_roots": [str(path) for path in scan_roots],
550.         "kind": args.kind,
551.         "granularity": args.granularity,
552.         "node_count": len(nodes),
553.         "edge_count": len(edges),
554.         "artifacts": [str(path) for path in written_paths],
555.     }
556.     print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
557.     return 0
558. 
559. 
560. if __name__ == "__main__":
561.     raise SystemExit(main())
562.

15. flake8 test_intelligent_data_detective.py --max-line-length=88 --extend-ignore=E203,E501
16. ```
17. 
18. **Full workflow execution requires API keys and takes 6–25 minutes. Never cancel it.**
19. 
20. ```bash
21. export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-api-key"
22. export TAVILY_API_KEY="your-tavily-api-key"  # Optional – enables web search
23. 
24. jupyter notebook IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb
25. ```
26. 
27. ## Architecture
28. 
29. The entire system lives in `IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb` (27 cells, ~11 k lines). There is no separate Python package; the notebook is the source of truth. Key cells:
30. 
31. | Cell | Purpose |
32. |------|---------|
33. | 1 | Environment setup, API key handling, package install |
34. | 4 | Core imports and type aliases |
35. | 5 | `MyChatOpenai` – custom `ChatOpenAI` subclass for GPT-5 / o-series models |
36. | 7 | Pydantic models (`BaseNoExtrasModel`, `State`, `AnalysisConfig`, etc.) |
37. | 8 | `DataFrameRegistry` – thread-safe LRU DataFrame manager |
38. | 10 | Agent prompt templates and `DEFAULT_TOOLING_GUIDELINES` |
39. | 12/13 | All tools (~78 functions) + `@handle_tool_errors` decorator |
40. | 14+ | Agent construction, LangGraph graph wiring, graph compilation |
41. 
42. **Agent pipeline** (supervisor-worker pattern via LangGraph):
43. 
44. ```
45. Supervisor → Initial Analysis → Data Cleaner → Analyst → Visualization
46.           → Report Orchestrator → Section Workers → Report Packager → File Writer
47. ```
48. 
49. The `State` TypedDict is the shared state object passed through every node. Agents communicate back to the supervisor via `reply_msg_to_supervisor`, `finished_this_task`, and `expect_reply` fields on their response models.
50. 
51. ## Key Conventions
52. 
53. ### Pydantic models for agent responses
54. All agent output models extend `BaseNoExtrasModel` (`model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`), which requires three base fields: `reply_msg_to_supervisor: str`, `finished_this_task: bool`, `expect_reply: bool`. Omitting any of these breaks supervisor routing.
55. 
56. ### State reducers
57. The `State` TypedDict uses custom reducers instead of plain annotations. Examples:
58. - `Annotated[Optional[AnalysisConfig], keep_first]` – first non-None value wins; never overwritten
59. - `Annotated[Optional[Plan], _reduce_plan_keep_sorted]` – merge-sorted plan steps
60. - `Annotated[Sequence[BaseMessage], operator.add]` – messages accumulate (standard LangGraph pattern)
61. 
62. Do not use plain field assignments for state fields that have these reducers, or state merges will silently behave incorrectly.
63. 
64. ### Tool implementation pattern
65. Every tool in Cell 13 follows this signature and decorator:
66. ```python
67. @handle_tool_errors
68. def my_tool(df_id: str, ...) -> tuple[str, dict]:
69.     validate_dataframe_exists(df_id)  # raises on invalid
70.     ...
71.     return result_message, artifact_dict
72. ```
73. `@handle_tool_errors` catches exceptions and returns a standardised error string so the agent can recover. `validate_dataframe_exists()` must be the first call in any tool that touches a DataFrame.
74. 
75. ### Tool list construction
76. The per-agent tool lists (`data_cleaning_tools`, `analyst_tools`, `visualization_tools`, etc.) are defined as empty lists early in Cell 13, then populated incrementally with `.append()` / `.extend()` throughout the cell. Tools appear after their function definitions. When adding a new tool, register it in the correct list at the point of definition.
77. 
78. ### DataFrameRegistry
79. `DataFrameRegistry` (Cell 8) is the single source of truth for all DataFrames. It uses `threading.RLock` internally. DataFrames are referenced everywhere by a string `df_id` (UUID or custom). Use `registry.register_dataframe(df, df_id)` to add, `registry.get_dataframe(df_id, load_if_not_exists=True)` to retrieve, which will reload from the stored CSV path on a cache miss.
80. 
81. ### MyChatOpenai
82. `MyChatOpenai` (Cell 5) overrides `_get_request_payload_mod` to handle o-series model quirks and the OpenAI Responses API. Use `MyChatOpenai` everywhere in the notebook instead of `ChatOpenAI` directly.
83. 
84. ### Memory namespaces
85. Memory is stored under categorised namespaces: `('memories', '<kind>')` where kind ∈ `{conversation, analysis, cleaning, visualization, insights, errors}`. TTL and per-kind limits are driven by `memory_config.yaml`, not hardcoded. Each agent is mapped to a subset of kinds in that file. When adding a new agent, add its `memory_kinds` mapping there.
86. 
87. ### File writes
88. All file-writing tools call `_resolve_artifact_path()` which validates that the target is within the artifacts directory (path-traversal protection). Never bypass this by writing directly with `open()`.
89. 
90. ## Known Issues
91. 
92. - `test_error_handling_framework.py`: one test fails due to an edge case in function-signature introspection. This is pre-existing and has no runtime impact.
93. - `flake8` reports some whitespace warnings on test files; these are acceptable.
````

42.     pattern = re.compile(

44.         r"<!-- repo-agent-bootstrap:provenance=.*?-->\s*"
45.         r"<!-- repo-agent-bootstrap:managed:start -->.*?<!-- repo-agent-bootstrap:managed:end -->\n?",
46.         re.DOTALL,
47.     )
48.     match = pattern.search(text)
49.     if not match:

51.     return match.start(), match.end(), match.group(0)

1. # Intelligent Data Detective - GitHub Copilot Instructions
2. 
3. ## Build, Test, and Lint
4. 
5. ```bash
6. # Run all tests
7. python3 -m pytest -v
8. # Expected: 22/22 pass in test_intelligent_data_detective.py, 15/16 in test_error_handling_framework.py (1 known edge-case failure)
9. 
10. # Run a single test
11. python3 -m pytest test_intelligent_data_detective.py::TestDataFrameRegistry::test_cache_lru_eviction -v
12. 
13. # Format and lint
14. black test_intelligent_data_detective.py test_error_handling_framework.py
15. flake8 test_intelligent_data_detective.py --max-line-length=88 --extend-ignore=E203,E501
16. ```
17. 
18. **Full workflow execution requires API keys and takes 6–25 minutes. Never cancel it.**
19. 
20. ```bash
21. export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-openai-api-key"
22. export TAVILY_API_KEY="your-tavily-api-key"  # Optional – enables web search
23. 
24. jupyter notebook IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb
25. ```
26. 
27. ## Architecture
28. 
29. The entire system lives in `IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb` (27 cells, ~11 k lines). There is no separate Python package; the notebook is the source of truth. Key cells:
30. 
31. | Cell | Purpose |
32. |------|---------|
33. | 1 | Environment setup, API key handling, package install |
34. | 4 | Core imports and type aliases |
35. | 5 | `MyChatOpenai` – custom `ChatOpenAI` subclass for GPT-5 / o-series models |
36. | 7 | Pydantic models (`BaseNoExtrasModel`, `State`, `AnalysisConfig`, etc.) |
37. | 8 | `DataFrameRegistry` – thread-safe LRU DataFrame manager |
38. | 10 | Agent prompt templates and `DEFAULT_TOOLING_GUIDELINES` |
39. | 12/13 | All tools (~78 functions) + `@handle_tool_errors` decorator |
40. | 14+ | Agent construction, LangGraph graph wiring, graph compilation |
41. 
42. **Agent pipeline** (supervisor-worker pattern via LangGraph):
43. 
44. ```
45. Supervisor → Initial Analysis → Data Cleaner → Analyst → Visualization
46.           → Report Orchestrator → Section Workers → Report Packager → File Writer
47. ```
48. 
49. The `State` TypedDict is the shared state object passed through every node. Agents communicate back to the supervisor via `reply_msg_to_supervisor`, `finished_this_task`, and `expect_reply` fields on their response models.
50. 
51. ## Key Conventions
52. 
53. ### Pydantic models for agent responses
54. All agent output models extend `BaseNoExtrasModel` (`model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`), which requires three base fields: `reply_msg_to_supervisor: str`, `finished_this_task: bool`, `expect_reply: bool`. Omitting any of these breaks supervisor routing.
55. 
56. ### State reducers
57. The `State` TypedDict uses custom reducers instead of plain annotations. Examples:
58. - `Annotated[Optional[AnalysisConfig], keep_first]` – first non-None value wins; never overwritten
59. - `Annotated[Optional[Plan], _reduce_plan_keep_sorted]` – merge-sorted plan steps
60. - `Annotated[Sequence[BaseMessage], operator.add]` – messages accumulate (standard LangGraph pattern)
61. 
62. Do not use plain field assignments for state fields that have these reducers, or state merges will silently behave incorrectly.
63. 
64. ### Tool implementation pattern
65. Every tool in Cell 13 follows this signature and decorator:
66. ```python
67. @handle_tool_errors
68. def my_tool(df_id: str, ...) -> tuple[str, dict]:
69.     validate_dataframe_exists(df_id)  # raises on invalid
70.     ...
71.     return result_message, artifact_dict
72. ```
73. `@handle_tool_errors` catches exceptions and returns a standardised error string so the agent can recover. `validate_dataframe_exists()` must be the first call in any tool that touches a DataFrame.
74. 
75. ### Tool list construction
76. The per-agent tool lists (`data_cleaning_tools`, `analyst_tools`, `visualization_tools`, etc.) are defined as empty lists early in Cell 13, then populated incrementally with `.append()` / `.extend()` throughout the cell. Tools appear after their function definitions. When adding a new tool, register it in the correct list at the point of definition.
77. 
78. ### DataFrameRegistry
79. `DataFrameRegistry` (Cell 8) is the single source of truth for all DataFrames. It uses `threading.RLock` internally. DataFrames are referenced everywhere by a string `df_id` (UUID or custom). Use `registry.register_dataframe(df, df_id)` to add, `registry.get_dataframe(df_id, load_if_not_exists=True)` to retrieve, which will reload from the stored CSV path on a cache miss.
80. 
81. ### MyChatOpenai
82. `MyChatOpenai` (Cell 5) overrides `_get_request_payload_mod` to handle o-series model quirks and the OpenAI Responses API. Use `MyChatOpenai` everywhere in the notebook instead of `ChatOpenAI` directly.
83. 
84. ### Memory namespaces
85. Memory is stored under categorised namespaces: `('memories', '<kind>')` where kind ∈ `{conversation, analysis, cleaning, visualization, insights, errors}`. TTL and per-kind limits are driven by `memory_config.yaml`, not hardcoded. Each agent is mapped to a subset of kinds in that file. When adding a new agent, add its `memory_kinds` mapping there.
86. 
87. ### File writes
88. All file-writing tools call `_resolve_artifact_path()` which validates that the target is within the artifacts directory (path-traversal protection). Never bypass this by writing directly with `open()`.
89. 
90. ## Known Issues
91. 
92. - `test_error_handling_framework.py`: one test fails due to an edge case in function-signature introspection. This is pre-existing and has no runtime impact.
93. - `flake8` reports some whitespace warnings on test files; these are acceptable.
94.

1. # Unit Testing Patterns for LangGraph Agents
2. 
3. This reference provides comprehensive patterns for writing unit tests for LangGraph agents in both Python and JavaScript/TypeScript.
4. 
5. ## Table of Contents
6. 
7. - [Testing Individual Nodes](#testing-individual-nodes)
8. - [Testing State Transitions](#testing-state-transitions)
9. - [Mocking LLM Responses](#mocking-llm-responses)
10. - [Testing Tool Calls](#testing-tool-calls)
11. - [Testing Conditional Edges](#testing-conditional-edges)
12. - [Pytest Patterns](#pytest-patterns)
13. - [Vitest/Jest Patterns](#vitestjest-patterns)
14. 
15. ## Testing Individual Nodes
16. 
17. ### Python Example (Pytest)
18. 
19. ```python
20. import pytest
21. from your_agent import agent_node, AgentState
22. 
23. def test_agent_node_basic():
24.     """Test agent node with simple input."""
25.     state = AgentState(
26.         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
27.     )
28. 
29.     result = agent_node(state)
30. 
31.     assert "messages" in result
32.     assert len(result["messages"]) > 0
33.     assert result["messages"][-1]["role"] == "assistant"
34. 
35. def test_agent_node_with_tools():
36.     """Test agent node that should call tools."""
37.     state = AgentState(
38.         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather?"}]
39.     )
40. 
41.     result = agent_node(state)
42. 
43.     # Verify tool call was made
44.     assert any(
45.         "tool_calls" in msg
46.         for msg in result["messages"]
47.     )
48. ```
49. 
50. ### TypeScript Example (Vitest)
51. 
52. ```typescript
53. import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
54. import { agentNode, type AgentState } from "./your-agent";
55. 
56. describe("Agent Node", () => {
57.   it("should process basic input", () => {
58.     const state: AgentState = {
59.       messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hello" }],
60.     };
61. 
62.     const result = agentNode(state);
63. 
64.     expect(result.messages).toBeDefined();
65.     expect(result.messages.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
66.     expect(result.messages[result.messages.length - 1].role).toBe("assistant");
67.   });
68. 
69.   it("should call tools when needed", () => {
70.     const state: AgentState = {
71.       messages: [{ role: "user", content: "What's the weather?" }],
72.     };
73. 
74.     const result = agentNode(state);
75. 
76.     const hasToolCall = result.messages.some((msg) => "tool_calls" in msg);
77.     expect(hasToolCall).toBe(true);
78.   });
79. });
80. ```
81. 
82. ## Testing State Transitions
83. 
84. ### Python Example
85. 
86. ```python
87. def test_state_accumulation():
88.     """Test that state accumulates correctly across nodes."""
89.     initial_state = AgentState(
90.         messages=[],
91.         metadata={"step": 0}
92.     )
93. 
94.     # First node
95.     state1 = node_a(initial_state)
96.     assert state1["metadata"]["step"] == 1
97. 
98.     # Second node
99.     state2 = node_b(state1)
100.     assert state2["metadata"]["step"] == 2
101.     assert len(state2["messages"]) > 0
102. 
103. def test_reducer_behavior():
104.     """Test custom reducer functions."""
105.     from operator import add
106. 
107.     state = {"items": [1, 2, 3]}
108.     new_items = [4, 5]
109. 
110.     # Test list concatenation reducer
111.     result = add(state["items"], new_items)
112.     assert result == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
113. ```
114. 
115. ### TypeScript Example
116. 
117. ```typescript
118. describe("State Transitions", () => {
119.   it("should accumulate state correctly", () => {
120.     const initialState: AgentState = {
121.       messages: [],
122.       metadata: { step: 0 },
123.     };
124. 
125.     // First node
126.     const state1 = nodeA(initialState);
127.     expect(state1.metadata.step).toBe(1);
128. 
129.     // Second node
130.     const state2 = nodeB(state1);
131.     expect(state2.metadata.step).toBe(2);
132.     expect(state2.messages.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
133.   });
134. });
135. ```

137. ## Mocking LLM Responses
138. 
139. ### Python Example with Mock
140. 
141. ```python
142. from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
143. 
144. def test_with_mocked_llm():
145.     """Test agent with mocked LLM responses."""
146.     mock_llm = Mock()
147.     mock_llm.invoke.return_value = {
148.         "role": "assistant",
149.         "content": "Mocked response"
150.     }
151. 
152.     # Inject mock into agent
153.     with patch('your_agent.llm', mock_llm):
154.         state = AgentState(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}])
155.         result = agent_node(state)
156. 
157.         assert mock_llm.invoke.called
158.         assert result["messages"][-1]["content"] == "Mocked response"
159. 
160. def test_with_tool_calls():
161.     """Test mocked LLM that returns tool calls."""
162.     mock_llm = Mock()
163.     mock_llm.invoke.return_value = {
164.         "role": "assistant",
165.         "content": "",
166.         "tool_calls": [
167.             {
168.                 "name": "search",
169.                 "args": {"query": "weather"},
170.                 "id": "call_123"
171.             }
172.         ]
173.     }
174. 
175.     with patch('your_agent.llm', mock_llm):
176.         state = AgentState(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Weather?"}])
177.         result = agent_node(state)
178. 
179.         assert len(result["messages"][-1]["tool_calls"]) == 1
180.         assert result["messages"][-1]["tool_calls"][0]["name"] == "search"
181. ```
182. 
183. ### TypeScript Example with Vi
184. 
185. ```typescript
186. import { vi } from "vitest";
187. 
188. describe("Mocked LLM Tests", () => {
189.   it("should work with mocked LLM responses", async () => {

193.         content: "Mocked response",
194.       }),
195.     };
196. 
197.     const state: AgentState = {
198.       messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hi" }],
199.     };
200. 
201.     const result = await agentNode(state, mockLLM);
202. 
203.     expect(mockLLM.invoke).toHaveBeenCalled();
204.     expect(result.messages[result.messages.length - 1].content).toBe(
205.       "Mocked response"
206.     );
207.   });
208. 
209.   it("should handle tool calls", async () => {
210.     const mockLLM = {
211.       invoke: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
212.         role: "assistant",
213.         content: "",
214.         tool_calls: [
215.           {
216.             name: "search",
217.             args: { query: "weather" },
218.             id: "call_123",
219.           },
220.         ],
221.       }),
222.     };
223. 
224.     const state: AgentState = {
225.       messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Weather?" }],
226.     };
227. 
228.     const result = await agentNode(state, mockLLM);
229. 
230.     expect(result.messages[result.messages.length - 1].tool_calls).toHaveLength(1);
231.     expect(result.messages[result.messages.length - 1].tool_calls[0].name).toBe(
232.       "search"
233.     );
234.   });
235. });
236. ```

238. ## Testing Tool Calls
239. 
240. ### Python Example
241. 
242. ```python
243. def test_tool_execution():
244.     """Test that tools execute correctly."""
245.     from your_agent import search_tool
246. 
247.     result = search_tool("weather in San Francisco")
248. 
249.     assert result is not None
250.     assert "temperature" in result or "forecast" in result
251. 
252. def test_tool_error_handling():
253.     """Test tool error handling."""
254.     from your_agent import search_tool
255. 
256.     # Test with invalid input
257.     result = search_tool("")
258. 
259.     # Should return error message, not raise exception
260.     assert "error" in result.lower() or result is None
261. ```
262. 
263. ### TypeScript Example
264. 
265. ```typescript

267.   it("should execute tool correctly", async () => {

269. 
270.     expect(result).toBeDefined();
271.     expect(
272.       result.includes("temperature") || result.includes("forecast")
273.     ).toBe(true);
274.   });
275. 
276.   it("should handle tool errors gracefully", async () => {
277.     const result = await searchTool("");
278. 
279.     // Should return error message, not throw
280.     expect(result.toLowerCase()).toContain("error");
281.   });
282. });
283. ```

285. ## Testing Conditional Edges
286. 
287. ### Python Example
288. 
289. ```python
290. def test_routing_logic():
291.     """Test conditional edge routing."""
292.     from your_agent import should_continue, AgentState
293. 
294.     # State with tool calls should continue
295.     state_with_tools = AgentState(
296.         messages=[
297.             {
298.                 "role": "assistant",
299.                 "tool_calls": [{"name": "search"}]
300.             }
301.         ]
302.     )
303. 
304.     assert should_continue(state_with_tools) == "continue"
305. 
306.     # State without tool calls should end
307.     state_without_tools = AgentState(
308.         messages=[
309.             {
310.                 "role": "assistant",
311.                 "content": "Final answer"
312.             }
313.         ]
314.     )
315. 
316.     assert should_continue(state_without_tools) == "end"
317. 
318. def test_router_selects_correct_node():
319.     """Test router function."""
320.     from your_agent import route_to_specialist
321. 
322.     math_state = AgentState(
323.         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}]
324.     )
325.     assert route_to_specialist(math_state) == "math_agent"
326. 
327.     code_state = AgentState(
328.         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a function"}]
329.     )
330.     assert route_to_specialist(code_state) == "code_agent"
331. ```
332.

375. ## Pytest Patterns
376. 
377. ### Fixtures
378. 
379. ```python
380. import pytest
381. from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver
382. 
383. @pytest.fixture
384. def memory_saver():
385.     """Provide a fresh memory saver for each test."""
386.     return MemorySaver()
387. 
388. @pytest.fixture
389. def compiled_graph(memory_saver):
390.     """Provide a compiled graph with memory."""
391.     from your_agent import build_graph
392. 
393.     graph = build_graph()
394.     return graph.compile(checkpointer=memory_saver)
395. 
396. @pytest.fixture
397. def mock_llm():
398.     """Provide a mocked LLM."""
399.     from unittest.mock import Mock
400. 
401.     mock = Mock()
402.     mock.invoke.return_value = {
403.         "role": "assistant",
404.         "content": "Test response"
405.     }
406.     return mock
407. ```
408. 
409. ### Parametrized Tests
410. 
411. ```python
412. @pytest.mark.parametrize("input_text,expected_node", [
413.     ("What's 2+2?", "math_agent"),
414.     ("Write code", "code_agent"),
415.     ("General question", "general_agent"),
416. ])
417. def test_routing_parametrized(input_text, expected_node):
418.     """Test routing with multiple inputs."""
419.     state = AgentState(
420.         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": input_text}]
421.     )
422. 
423.     result = route_to_specialist(state)
424.     assert result == expected_node
425. ```
426. 
427. ### Test Caching
428. 
429. ```python
430. # pytest.ini or pyproject.toml
431. # [tool.pytest.ini_options]
432. # cache_dir = "tests/.pytest_cache"
433. 
434. # Use with LangSmith test cache
435. import os
436. os.environ["LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE"] = "tests/cassettes"
437. 
438. @pytest.mark.llm  # Mark tests that use real LLMs
439. def test_with_real_llm(compiled_graph):
440.     """Test with real LLM (cached)."""
441.     state = {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}
442. 
443.     result = compiled_graph.invoke(state)
444.     assert len(result["messages"]) > 1
445. ```
446. 
447. ## Vitest/Jest Patterns
448. 
449. ### Setup Files
450. 
451. ```typescript
452. // vitest.config.ts
453. import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";
454. 
455. export default defineConfig({
456.   test: {
457.     globals: true,
458.     environment: "node",
459.     setupFiles: ["./tests/setup.ts"],
460.   },
461. });
462. 
463. // tests/setup.ts
464. import { beforeEach, vi } from "vitest";
465. 
466. beforeEach(() => {
467.   // Reset mocks before each test
468.   vi.clearAllMocks();
469. });
470. ```
471. 
472. ### Parameterized Tests
473. 
474. ```typescript
475. describe.each([
476.   ["What's 2+2?", "math_agent"],
477.   ["Write code", "code_agent"],
478.   ["General question", "general_agent"],
479. ])("Routing with input: %s", (inputText, expectedNode) => {
480.   it(`should route to ${expectedNode}`, () => {
481.     const state: AgentState = {
482.       messages: [{ role: "user", content: inputText }],
483.     };
484. 
485.     const result = routeToSpecialist(state);
486.     expect(result).toBe(expectedNode);
487.   });
488. });
489. ```
490. 
491. ### Snapshot Testing
492. 
493. ```typescript
494. it("should match snapshot", () => {
495.   const state: AgentState = {
496.     messages: [{ role: "user", "content": "Test input" }],
497.   };
498. 
499.   const result = processState(state);
500. 
501.   expect(result).toMatchSnapshot();
502. });
503. ```
504. 
505. ## Best Practices
506. 
507. 1. **Test isolation**: Each test should be independent
508. 2. **Mock external dependencies**: Always mock LLM calls in unit tests
509. 3. **Test edge cases**: Empty inputs, invalid data, error conditions
510. 4. **Use descriptive test names**: Make failures easy to understand
511. 5. **Keep tests fast**: Unit tests should run in milliseconds
512. 6. **Test one thing**: Each test should verify a single behavior
513. 7. **Use fixtures/setup**: Reduce duplication across tests
514. 8. **Test both success and failure paths**: Don't just test happy paths
515.
````

</details>

1. # Trajectory Evaluation for LangGraph Agents
2. 
3. Trajectory evaluation assesses the sequence of actions and decisions an agent makes, not just the final output. This is critical for multi-step reasoning agents where the execution path matters.
4. 
5. ## Table of Contents
6. 
7. - [What is Trajectory Evaluation](#what-is-trajectory-evaluation)
8. - [Trajectory Match Evaluator](#trajectory-match-evaluator)
9. - [LLM-as-Judge Evaluator](#llm-as-judge-evaluator)
10. - [Creating Datasets](#creating-datasets)
11. - [Using AgentEvals with LangSmith](#using-agentevals-with-langsmith)
12. - [Best Practices](#best-practices)
13. - [Common Patterns](#common-patterns)
14. 
15. ## What is Trajectory Evaluation
16. 
17. A trajectory is the complete sequence of:
18. - Messages exchanged
19. - Tool calls made
20. - Decisions at conditional edges
21. - State transformations
22. 
23. Output-only evaluation misses important quality signals like:
24. - Did the agent call the right tools?
25. - Were tools called in a logical order?
26. - Did the agent make unnecessary steps?
27. - Was the reasoning process sound?
28. 
29. ## Trajectory Match Evaluator
30. 
31. Use trajectory match when you want deterministic validation against a reference trajectory.
32. 
33. AgentEvals supports four match modes:
34. - `strict`: exact sequence match
35. - `unordered`: same tool calls, order does not matter
36. - `subset`: no tool calls outside reference
37. - `superset`: includes all required reference tool calls (extras allowed)
38. 
39. ### Python Example
40. 
41. ```python
42. from langchain.messages import HumanMessage, AIMessage, ToolMessage
43. from agentevals.trajectory.match import create_trajectory_match_evaluator
44. 
45. # Strict match of the trajectory
46. trajectory_evaluator = create_trajectory_match_evaluator(
47.     trajectory_match_mode="strict"
48. )
49. 
50. reference_trajectory = [
51.     HumanMessage(content="What's the weather in San Francisco?"),
52.     AIMessage(
53.         content="",
54.         tool_calls=[
55.             {"id": "call_1", "name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "San Francisco"}}
56.         ],
57.     ),
58.     ToolMessage(content="It's 72F and sunny in San Francisco.", tool_call_id="call_1"),
59.     AIMessage(content="The weather in San Francisco is 72F and sunny."),
60. ]
61. 
62. result = agent.invoke({
63.     "messages": [HumanMessage(content="What's the weather in San Francisco?")]
64. })
65. 
66. evaluation = trajectory_evaluator(
67.     outputs=result["messages"],
68.     reference_outputs=reference_trajectory,
69. )
70. 
71. assert evaluation["score"] is True
72. ```
73. 
74. ### TypeScript Example
75. 
76. ```typescript

78. import { createTrajectoryMatchEvaluator } from "agentevals";
79. 
80. const trajectoryEvaluator = createTrajectoryMatchEvaluator({
81.   trajectoryMatchMode: "strict",
82. });
83. 
84. const referenceTrajectory = [
85.   new HumanMessage("What's the weather in San Francisco?"),
86.   new AIMessage({
87.     content: "",
88.     tool_calls: [{ id: "call_1", name: "get_weather", args: { city: "San Francisco" } }],
89.   }),
90.   new ToolMessage({
91.     content: "It's 72F and sunny in San Francisco.",
92.     tool_call_id: "call_1",
93.   }),
94.   new AIMessage("The weather in San Francisco is 72F and sunny."),
95. ];
96. 
97. const result = await agent.invoke({
98.   messages: [new HumanMessage("What's the weather in San Francisco?")],
99. });
100. 
101. const evaluation = await trajectoryEvaluator({
102.   outputs: result.messages,
103.   referenceOutputs: referenceTrajectory,
104. });
105. 
106. expect(evaluation.score).toBe(true);

109. ## LLM-as-Judge Evaluator
110. 
111. Use LLM-as-judge when multiple trajectories may be valid and you want qualitative scoring.
112. 
113. ### Python Example
114. 
115. ```python
116. from agentevals.trajectory.llm import (
117.     create_trajectory_llm_as_judge,
118.     TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT,
119.     TRAJECTORY_EFFICIENCY_PROMPT,
120.     TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT_WITH_REFERENCE,
121. )
122. 
123. accuracy_evaluator = create_trajectory_llm_as_judge(
124.     model="openai:o3-mini",
125.     prompt=TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT,
126. )
127. 
128. efficiency_evaluator = create_trajectory_llm_as_judge(
129.     model="openai:o3-mini",
130.     prompt=TRAJECTORY_EFFICIENCY_PROMPT,
131. )
132. 
133. with_reference_evaluator = create_trajectory_llm_as_judge(
134.     model="openai:o3-mini",
135.     prompt=TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT_WITH_REFERENCE,
136. )
137. 
138. result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Seattle?"}]})
139. 
140. evaluation = accuracy_evaluator(outputs=result["messages"])
141. # If you have a reference trajectory, use reference_outputs:
142. # evaluation = with_reference_evaluator(outputs=result["messages"], reference_outputs=reference_trajectory)
143. 
144. assert evaluation["score"] is True

262. ## Using AgentEvals with LangSmith
263.

347. ## Best Practices
348. 
349. 1. Start with deterministic trajectory matching for well-defined flows.
350. 2. Use LLM-as-judge when multiple trajectories can be correct.
351. 3. Prefer `openai:o3-mini` (or another current evaluator model) for judge evaluators.
352. 4. Version trajectory datasets as your agent behavior evolves.
353. 5. Include edge cases and failure paths in trajectory datasets.
354. 6. Track evaluation cost and latency for LLM-as-judge runs.
355. 7. Inspect failed runs in LangSmith traces, not just aggregate scores.
356. 8. Keep evaluator prompts explicit and stable over time.
357. 
358. ## Common Patterns
359. 
360. ### Tool Call Validation
361. 
362. ```python
363. def validate_tool_calls(run, example):
364.     """Custom evaluator for tool call validation."""
365.     messages = run.outputs.get("messages", [])
366.     expected_tools = example.metadata.get("expected_tools", [])
367. 
368.     actual_tools = []
369.     for msg in messages:
370.         for tool_call in msg.get("tool_calls", []):
371.             actual_tools.append(tool_call["name"])
372. 
373.     score = 1.0 if set(expected_tools).issubset(set(actual_tools)) else 0.0
374. 
375.     return {
376.         "key": "tool_call_validation",
377.         "score": score,
378.         "comment": f"Expected: {expected_tools}, Actual: {actual_tools}",
379.     }
380. ```
381. 
382. ### Compare Two Agent Versions
383. 
384. ```python
385. from langsmith import Client
386. 
387. client = Client()
388. 
389. results_v1 = client.evaluate(agent_v1, data="test_dataset", evaluators=[evaluator], experiment_prefix="v1")
390. results_v2 = client.evaluate(agent_v2, data="test_dataset", evaluators=[evaluator], experiment_prefix="v2")
391. 
392. exp_v1 = client.read_project(project_name=results_v1.experiment_name, include_stats=True)
393. exp_v2 = client.read_project(project_name=results_v2.experiment_name, include_stats=True)
394. 
395. print("V1 feedback stats:", exp_v1.feedback_stats)
396. print("V2 feedback stats:", exp_v2.feedback_stats)
397. ```
398.
