234. def persist_to_drive(
235.     src: PathlibPath,
236.     run_id: Optional[str] = None,
237.     dst_root: Optional[PathlibPath] = None,
238.     ignore_names: Iterable[str] = ("__pycache__", ".git", "node_modules"),
239. ) -> PathlibPath:
240.     """
241.     Copy a file or directory into the IDD_results/IDD_run_<date>_<run_id> folder.
242.     Returns the destination run folder path.
243.     """
244.     src = PathlibPath(src)
245.     if not src.exists():
246.         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source does not exist: {src}")
247. 
248.     if dst_root is None:
249.         ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
250.         run_id = run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
251.         dst_root = _make_idd_results_dir() / f"IDD_run_{run_id}"
252.         dst_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
253.     else:
254.         dst_root = PathlibPath(dst_root)
255.         dst_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
256. 
257.     # Prevent copying the destination into itself
258.     if _is_relative_to(src, dst_root):
259.         raise ValueError(f"Refusing to copy {src} into its own destination {dst_root}")
260. 
261.     def _should_ignore(name: str) -> bool:
262.         return name in ignore_names
263. 
264.     if src.is_dir():
265.         for item in src.iterdir():
266.             if _should_ignore(item.name):
267.                 continue
268.             target = dst_root / item.name
269.             if item.is_dir():
270.                 shutil.copytree(item, target, dirs_exist_ok=True, symlinks=True)
271.             else:
272.                 target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
273.                 shutil.copy2(item, target)
274.     else:
275.         target = dst_root / src.name
276.         target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
277.         shutil.copy2(src, target)
278.

1272. def merge_int_sum(a: int | None, b: int | None) -> int:
1273.     return int(a or 0) + int(b or 0)
1274. 
1275. def merge_dicts(a: Dict | None, b: Dict | None) -> Dict:

1277.     if a: d.update(a)
1278.     if b: d.update(b)
1279.     return d
1280.

1282. # Reducers (how to merge when parallel branches rejoin)
1283. def merge_dict(a: Optional[dict], b: Optional[dict]) -> dict:
1284.     return {**(a or {}), **(b or {})}
1285. 
1286. def any_true(a: Optional[bool], b: Optional[bool]) -> bool:
1287.     return bool(a) or bool(b)

1289. def last_wins(a, b):

1291.     return b
1292. def _reduce_plan_keep_sorted(a: Optional[Plan], b: Optional[Plan]) -> Optional[Plan]:
1293.     if a is None: return b
1294.     if b is None: return a
1295. 
1296.     # Merge (last-wins for non-list fields). For steps: concat, dedup by step_number, then sort.
1297.     steps = []
1298.     if a.plan_steps: steps.extend(a.plan_steps)
1299.     if b.plan_steps: steps.extend(b.plan_steps)
1300. 
1301.     # normalize and dedup by step_number (keep later value = from b)
1302.     norm = [s if isinstance(s, PlanStep) else PlanStep.model_validate(s) for s in steps]
1303.     by_num = {s.step_number: s for s in norm}  # last write wins
1304.     merged_sorted_steps = [by_num[k] for k in sorted(by_num)]
1305. 
1306.     merged = {**a.model_dump(), **b.model_dump(), "plan_steps": merged_sorted_steps}
1307.     return Plan.model_validate(merged)

302. def dict_merge_shallow(old: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], new: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
303.     """
304.     Merge two dicts shallowly (one level).
305.     - If both old and new are None, return {}.
306.     - If only one is non-empty, return that one.

463.             # responses api: {"type": "function", "name": "...", "description": "...", "parameters": {...}, "strict": ...}  # noqa: E501
464.             if tool["type"] == "function" and "function" in tool:

480.                     else:
481.                         pass
482. 
483.                 new_tools.append(tool)
484.

487.         # chat api: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}
488.         # responses api: {"type": "function", "name": "..."}

536.                 }

741. class QueryDataframeInput(BaseModel):
742.     """
743.     Args schema to query a registered DataFrame by columns, optional equality filter, and an operation.
744. 
745.     Parameter container class for Tool with name: query_dataframe
746.     Returns (content, artifact) with response_format="content_and_artifact".
747. 
748.     Args:
749.       params (DataQueryParams) is the only required parameter, with the following fields:
750.         - operation: one of {"select", "sum", "mean", "count"}.
751.         - columns: list[str] — target columns for the operation (must exist).
752.         - filter_column: Optional[str] — column to filter on (must exist if provided).
753.         - filter_value: Any — value to match when filter_column is set (equality match).
754.         - df_id (str): ID of a DataFrame in the global registry. If missing, the tool attempts to load it from the registry’s recorded raw path (CSV) and re‑register it.
755. 
756.     Behavior:
757.       - If filter_column is provided, rows are restricted to (df[filter_column] == filter_value).
758.       - Operations:
759.           • "select": returns list[dict] of row records for `columns`.
760.           • "sum":    returns dict {column: sum} over numeric cols (numeric_only=True).
761.           • "mean":   returns dict {column: mean} over numeric cols (numeric_only=True).
762.           • "count":  returns dict {column: non_null_count}.
763.       - On success, also registers the result as a new DataFrame with ID:
764.           f"{df_id}_{params.operation}_result"
765.         and returns that new ID in the artifact.
766. 
767.     Returns:
768.       tuple[str, dict]
769.         content:
770.           - "Query successful." on success
771.           - or "Error: ..." on recoverable failures (e.g., missing df, bad filter column, unsupported op)
772.         artifact:
773.           - success: {"result": <list|dict>, "df_id": <new_df_id>}
774.           - error:   {"error": <message>, "df_id": <original_df_id>}
775. 
776.     Notes for agents:
777.       - Provide valid existing column names in `params.columns` (the `columns` field of the params argument, which is of type DataQueryParams); invalid names may raise an exception.
778.       - Filtering is equality-only on a single column.
779.       - Large "select" results can be big; consider limiting columns or filtering first.
780.       - Some errors are returned as strings prefixed with "Error:", but unexpected exceptions are raised.
781.     """
782.     model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid",json_schema_extra={"additionalProperties": False})

234. def persist_to_drive(
235.     src: PathlibPath,
236.     run_id: Optional[str] = None,
237.     dst_root: Optional[PathlibPath] = None,
238.     ignore_names: Iterable[str] = ("__pycache__", ".git", "node_modules"),
239. ) -> PathlibPath:
240.     """
241.     Copy a file or directory into the IDD_results/IDD_run_<date>_<run_id> folder.
242.     Returns the destination run folder path.
243.     """
244.     src = PathlibPath(src)
245.     if not src.exists():
246.         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source does not exist: {src}")
247. 
248.     if dst_root is None:
249.         ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
250.         run_id = run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
251.         dst_root = _make_idd_results_dir() / f"IDD_run_{run_id}"
252.         dst_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
253.     else:
254.         dst_root = PathlibPath(dst_root)
255.         dst_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
256. 
257.     # Prevent copying the destination into itself
258.     if _is_relative_to(src, dst_root):
259.         raise ValueError(f"Refusing to copy {src} into its own destination {dst_root}")
260. 
261.     def _should_ignore(name: str) -> bool:
262.         return name in ignore_names
263. 
264.     if src.is_dir():
265.         for item in src.iterdir():
266.             if _should_ignore(item.name):
267.                 continue
268.             target = dst_root / item.name
269.             if item.is_dir():
270.                 shutil.copytree(item, target, dirs_exist_ok=True, symlinks=True)
271.             else:
272.                 target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
273.                 shutil.copy2(item, target)
274.     else:
275.         target = dst_root / src.name
276.         target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
277.         shutil.copy2(src, target)
278. 
279.     print(f"Persisted {src} -> {dst_root}")
280.     return dst_root

294. def keep_first(a: Optional[Any], b: Optional[Any]) -> Optional[Any]:
295.     """
296.     Reducer to preserve the first non-null value.
297.     If `a` is not None, returns a—not overridden by `b`.
298.     Else returns `b`.
299.     """
300.     return a if a is not None else b

302. def dict_merge_shallow(old: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], new: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
303.     """
304.     Merge two dicts shallowly (one level).
305.     - If both old and new are None, return {}.
306.     - If only one is non-empty, return that one.
307.     - If both exist, new keys override old.
308.     """
309.     if old is None and new is None:
310.         return {}
311.     if old is None:
312.         return dict(new)
313.     if new is None:
314.         return dict(old)
315.     return {**old, **new}

331. def is_1d_vector(x: object) -> TypeGuard[Array1D]:
332.     """
333.     Return True if x is a 1-D numeric-like sequence:
334.      - pandas.Series,
335.      - numpy.ndarray with ndim == 1,
336.      - list/tuple of scalars convertible to a 1-D array.
337.     """
338.     try:
339.         if isinstance(x, (str, bytes)):
340.             return False
341.         if isinstance(x, pd.Series):
342.             return True
343.         if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
344.             return x.ndim == 1
345.         if is_list_like(x):
346.             try:
347.                 arr = np.asarray(x)
348.             except Exception:
349.                 return False
350.             return arr.ndim == 1
351.         if isinstance(x, Sequence):
352.             try:
353.                 arr = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
354.             except (ValueError, TypeError):
355.                 return False
356.             return arr.ndim == 1
357.         return False
358.     except Exception as e:
359.         raise e

432. - **LangChain/LangGraph Stack**: Core imports for the multi-agent framework
433. - **Data Science Libraries**: Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn for data analysis
434. - **Type Safety**: Extensive use of TypedDict, Literal types, and generic annotations
435. 
436. # 🤖 OpenAI API Integration and Model Customization
437. """
438. 
439. from langchain_core.language_models import LanguageModelInput
440. from langchain_openai.chat_models.base import _construct_responses_api_input, _is_pydantic_class, _convert_message_to_dict, _convert_to_openai_response_format, _get_last_messages
441. from langchain_core.messages import BaseMessage
442. 
443. def _construct_responses_api_payload(
444.     messages: Sequence[BaseMessage], payload: dict
445. ) -> dict:
446.     # Rename legacy parameters
447.     for legacy_token_param in ["max_tokens", "max_completion_tokens"]:
448.         if legacy_token_param in payload:
449.             payload["max_output_tokens"] = payload.pop(legacy_token_param)
450.     if "reasoning_effort" in payload and "reasoning" not in payload:
451.         payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": payload.pop("reasoning_effort")}
452. 
453.     # Remove temperature parameter for models that don't support it in responses API
454.     model = payload.get("model", "")
455.     if model.startswith("gpt-5"):
456.         payload.pop("temperature", None)
457. 
458.     payload["input"] = _construct_responses_api_input(messages)
459.     if tools := payload.pop("tools", None):
460.         new_tools: list = []
461.         for tool in tools:
462.             # chat api: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "...", "description": "...", "parameters": {...}, "strict": ...}  # noqa: E501
463.             # responses api: {"type": "function", "name": "...", "description": "...", "parameters": {...}, "strict": ...}  # noqa: E501
464.             if tool["type"] == "function" and "function" in tool:
465.                 new_tools.append({"type": "function", **tool["function"]})
466.             else:
467.                 if tool["type"] == "image_generation":
468.                     # Handle partial images (not yet supported)
469.                     if "partial_images" in tool:
470.                         raise NotImplementedError(
471.                             "Partial image generation is not yet supported "
472.                             "via the LangChain ChatOpenAI client. Please "
473.                             "drop the 'partial_images' key from the image_generation "
474.                             "tool."
475.                         )
476.                     elif payload.get("stream") and "partial_images" not in tool:
477.                         # OpenAI requires this parameter be set; we ignore it during
478.                         # streaming.
479.                         tool["partial_images"] = 1
480.                     else:
481.                         pass
482. 
483.                 new_tools.append(tool)
484. 
485.         payload["tools"] = new_tools
486.     if tool_choice := payload.pop("tool_choice", None):
487.         # chat api: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}
488.         # responses api: {"type": "function", "name": "..."}
489.         if (
490.             isinstance(tool_choice, dict)
491.             and tool_choice["type"] == "function"
492.             and "function" in tool_choice
493.         ):
494.             payload["tool_choice"] = {"type": "function", **tool_choice["function"]}
495.         else:
496.             payload["tool_choice"] = tool_choice
497. 
498.     # Structured output
499.     if schema := payload.pop("response_format", None):
500.         existing_text = payload.pop("text", None)
501. 
502.         # For pydantic + non-streaming case, we use responses.parse.
503.         # Otherwise, we use responses.create.
504.         strict = payload.pop("strict", None)
505.         if not payload.get("stream") and _is_pydantic_class(schema):
506.             verbosity = payload.pop("verbosity", None)
507.             payload["text_format"] = schema
508. 
509.             text_content = (
510.                 existing_text.copy() if isinstance(existing_text, dict) else {}
511.             )
512.             if verbosity is not None:
513.                 text_content["verbosity"] = verbosity
514.             if text_content and "format" not in text_content:
515.                 payload["text"] = text_content
516.         else:
517.             # For responses.create, use response_format in text.format
518.             if _is_pydantic_class(schema):
519.                 schema_dict = schema.model_json_schema()
520.                 strict = True
521.             else:
522.                 schema_dict = schema
523.             if schema_dict == {"type": "json_object"}:  # JSON mode
524.                 structured_text = {"format": {"type": "json_object"}}
525.             elif (
526.                 (
527.                     response_format := _convert_to_openai_response_format(
528.                         schema_dict, strict=strict
529.                     )
530.                 )
531.                 and (isinstance(response_format, dict))
532.                 and (response_format["type"] == "json_schema")
533.             ):
534.                 structured_text = {
535.                     "format": {"type": "json_schema", **response_format["json_schema"]}
536.                 }
537.             else:
538.                 structured_text = {}
539. 
540.             # Merge existing text parameters with structured output text
541.             if existing_text or structured_text:
542.                 merged_text = {}
543.                 if existing_text and isinstance(existing_text, dict):
544.                     merged_text.update(existing_text)
545.                 if structured_text:
546.                     merged_text.update(structured_text)
547.                 payload["text"] = merged_text
548.             else:
549.                 pass
550. 
551.             # Handle verbosity for responses.create path
552.             verbosity = payload.pop("verbosity", None)
553.             if verbosity is not None:
554.                 if "text" not in payload:
555.                     payload["text"] = {"format": {"type": "text"}}
556.                 payload["text"]["verbosity"] = verbosity
557.     else:
558.         # No structured output, handle verbosity normally
559.         verbosity = payload.pop("verbosity", None)
560.         if verbosity is not None:
561.             if "text" not in payload:
562.                 payload["text"] = {"format": {"type": "text"}}
563.             payload["text"]["verbosity"] = verbosity
564. 
565.     return payload
566.

570. 
571.     def _get_request_payload_mod(
572.         self,
573.         input_: LanguageModelInput,
574.         *,
575.         stop: Optional[list[str]] = None,
576.         **kwargs: Any,
577.     ) -> dict:
578.         messages = self._convert_input(input_).to_messages()
579.         if stop is not None:
580.             kwargs["stop"] = stop
581. 
582.         payload = {**self._default_params, **kwargs}
583. 
584.         if self._use_responses_api(payload):
585.             if self.use_previous_response_id:
586.                 last_messages, previous_response_id = _get_last_messages(messages)
587.                 payload_to_use = last_messages if previous_response_id else messages
588.                 if previous_response_id:
589.                     payload["previous_response_id"] = previous_response_id
590.                 payload = _construct_responses_api_payload(payload_to_use, payload)
591.             else:
592.                 payload = _construct_responses_api_payload(messages, payload)
593.         else:
594.             payload["messages"] = [_convert_message_to_dict(m) for m in messages]
595.         return payload
596. 
597.     def _get_request_payload(
598.         self,
599.         input_: LanguageModelInput,
600.         *,
601.         stop: Optional[list[str]] = None,
602.         **kwargs: Any,
603.     ) -> dict:
604.         payload = self._get_request_payload_mod(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)
605.         # max_tokens was deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens
606.         # in September 2024 release
607.         if "max_tokens" in payload:
608.             payload["max_completion_tokens"] = payload.pop("max_tokens")
609. 
610.         # Mutate system message role to "developer" for o-series models
611.         if self.model_name and re.match(r"^o\d", self.model_name):
612.             for message in payload.get("messages", []):
613.                 if message["role"] == "system":
614.                     message["role"] = "developer"
615.         return payload

692.     Wrap both the image bytes and its declared MIME-type.

696. 
697.     @field_validator("payload", mode="before")
698.     def ensure_b64(cls, v: str | bytes):
699.         if isinstance(v, bytes):
700.             return v
701.         try:
702.             return base64.b64decode(v, validate=True)
703.         except Exception as e:
704.             raise ValueError("Invalid Base-64") from e
705. 
706.     @field_validator("payload")
707.     def enforce_size(cls, v: bytes):
708.         max_bytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024   # 2 MiB hard limit
709.         if len(v) > max_bytes:
710.             raise ValueError(f"Image is too large ({len(v)} bytes > {max_bytes})")
711.         return v

741. class QueryDataframeInput(BaseModel):
742.     """
743.     Args schema to query a registered DataFrame by columns, optional equality filter, and an operation.
744. 
745.     Parameter container class for Tool with name: query_dataframe
746.     Returns (content, artifact) with response_format="content_and_artifact".
747. 
748.     Args:
749.       params (DataQueryParams) is the only required parameter, with the following fields:
750.         - operation: one of {"select", "sum", "mean", "count"}.
751.         - columns: list[str] — target columns for the operation (must exist).
752.         - filter_column: Optional[str] — column to filter on (must exist if provided).
753.         - filter_value: Any — value to match when filter_column is set (equality match).
754.         - df_id (str): ID of a DataFrame in the global registry. If missing, the tool attempts to load it from the registry’s recorded raw path (CSV) and re‑register it.
755. 
756.     Behavior:
757.       - If filter_column is provided, rows are restricted to (df[filter_column] == filter_value).
758.       - Operations:
759.           • "select": returns list[dict] of row records for `columns`.
760.           • "sum":    returns dict {column: sum} over numeric cols (numeric_only=True).
761.           • "mean":   returns dict {column: mean} over numeric cols (numeric_only=True).
762.           • "count":  returns dict {column: non_null_count}.
763.       - On success, also registers the result as a new DataFrame with ID:
764.           f"{df_id}_{params.operation}_result"
765.         and returns that new ID in the artifact.
766. 
767.     Returns:
768.       tuple[str, dict]
769.         content:
770.           - "Query successful." on success
771.           - or "Error: ..." on recoverable failures (e.g., missing df, bad filter column, unsupported op)
772.         artifact:
773.           - success: {"result": <list|dict>, "df_id": <new_df_id>}
774.           - error:   {"error": <message>, "df_id": <original_df_id>}
775. 
776.     Notes for agents:
777.       - Provide valid existing column names in `params.columns` (the `columns` field of the params argument, which is of type DataQueryParams); invalid names may raise an exception.
778.       - Filtering is equality-only on a single column.
779.       - Large "select" results can be big; consider limiting columns or filtering first.
780.       - Some errors are returned as strings prefixed with "Error:", but unexpected exceptions are raised.
781.     """
782.     model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid",json_schema_extra={"additionalProperties": False})
783.     params: DataQueryParams
784.     # columns: List[str] = Field(..., description="List of columns to include in the output")
785.     # filter_column: str = Field(..., description="Column to apply the filter on")
786.     # filter_value: str = Field(..., description="Value to filter the rows by")
787.     # operation: str = Field(..., description="Operation to perform: 'select', 'sum', 'mean', 'count', 'max', 'min', 'median', etc.")
788.     df_id: str = Field(..., description="ID of the DataFrame in the registry")
789. class FileResult(BaseNoExtrasModel):
790.     """Results object storing metadata from the file generation or editing. The fields include the following:
791.     - write_success: Whether the file was written to disk successfully. If you did not succeed in writing the file to disk and do not have a viable file name and path to the file, then leave this field as False, and enter 'Failed to generate file' as the string for the 'file_path', 'file_type', 'file_name', and 'file_description' fields and 'error' in the 'category_tag' field. In the case of failed file writing or saving, use the 'reply_msg_to_supervisor' field to provide a more detailed error message to the supervisor and user, and set the 'finished_this_task' field to False and the 'expect_reply' field to True.
792.     - file_path: Path to the generated file. This is the accurate relative path to the actual file on disk, including the file name, as a string, and should be able used to read the file. The path should be relative to the working directory. Note the filename in the path should be match the 'file_name' field. Also note that after the last directory separator, the name of the file in file_path should match the 'file_name' field and the file extension of the file in file_path should match the 'file_type' field.
793.     - file_type: Type of the generated file. This is a string representing the actual type of the file or its format in terms of its file extension. Examples include 'csv', 'json', 'txt', 'png', 'pdf', 'html', 'md', 'parquet', 'xlsx', 'py', 'ipynb', 'pt', 'pkl', 'xml', 'sql', 'bytes', 'log', 'yml', 'db', or any other format supported by the file_writer agent's tools. Note that the file extension of the file in the 'file_path' field must match this file_type field.
794.     - file_name: Name of the generated file. This is a string representing the name of the file, without the file extension. Do not include the file extension in this field. Instead, indicate the file extension in the file_type field and include it in the full path in the file_path field. Of course, file_name should match the name of the file in the 'file_path' field after the last directory separator.
795.     - file_description: Description of the generated file. This is a string representing a brief and concisely worded but identifying description of the generated file that catalogues it effectively. It should be clear and concise and should include any relevant details about the file, such as its purpose, size, and any other relevant information such as the time and date it was generated, the type of data it contains, versioning information, how it was generated, how it can be used, etc.
796.     - is_final_report: Whether the file is the final report. Enter false if not final or if the file is not the final report or if the file any other file. Unless you know for sure you are writing the final report, leave this false.
797.     - category_tag: Type of the resulting file. This is a string representing the type of the resulting file, in terms of what category it falls under.
798.           Examples for each tag:
799.           'report': [report outline as a txt file, section of a report as txt or md file, the final report as a pdf, html, or markdown file]
800.           'data': [saved copy or transformation of a dataframe or series representing a particular column or subset of the dataset, a csv file, sql or db file, FAISS index or embeddings, pickled data, json config or data file, saved xlsx spreadsheets, parquet files, etc.]
801.           'visualization': [a specific chart, diagram or other visualization created saved as png or bytes image file, a saved mermaid file]
802.           'other': [any other type of file, files specifically requested by the user or supervisor or another agent, backed up files unrelated to the analysis or report, etc.]
803.           'error': This category tag is to only specifically be used when the file writing or saving process fails and the write_success field is set to False.
804.           For the category_tage field, use a SINGLE word only please, NO punctuation. Only enter one of: 'report', 'data', 'visualization', or 'other'.
805. 
806.     """

Set to True for a successful file generation, meaning you can provide the file path and other metadata in the relevant fields. 1292. def _reduce_plan_keep_sorted(a: Optional[Plan], b: Optional[Plan]) -> Optional[Plan]:
1293.     if a is None: return b
1294.     if b is None: return a
1295. 
1296.     # Merge (last-wins for non-list fields). For steps: concat, dedup by step_number, then sort.
1297.     steps = []
1298.     if a.plan_steps: steps.extend(a.plan_steps)
1299.     if b.plan_steps: steps.extend(b.plan_steps)
1300. 
1301.     # normalize and dedup by step_number (keep later value = from b)
1302.     norm = [s if isinstance(s, PlanStep) else PlanStep.model_validate(s) for s in steps]
1303.     by_num = {s.step_number: s for s in norm}  # last write wins
1304.     merged_sorted_steps = [by_num[k] for k in sorted(by_num)]
1305. 
1306.     merged = {**a.model_dump(), **b.model_dump(), "plan_steps": merged_sorted_steps}
1307.     return Plan.model_validate(merged)

234. def persist_to_drive(
235.     src: PathlibPath,
236.     run_id: Optional[str] = None,
237.     dst_root: Optional[PathlibPath] = None,
238.     ignore_names: Iterable[str] = ("__pycache__", ".git", "node_modules"),
239. ) -> PathlibPath:
240.     """
241.     Copy a file or directory into the IDD_results/IDD_run_<date>_<run_id> folder.
242.     Returns the destination run folder path.
243.     """
244.     src = PathlibPath(src)
245.     if not src.exists():
246.         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source does not exist: {src}")
247. 
248.     if dst_root is None:
249.         ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
250.         run_id = run_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
251.         dst_root = _make_idd_results_dir() / f"IDD_run_{run_id}"
252.         dst_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
253.     else:
254.         dst_root = PathlibPath(dst_root)
255.         dst_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
256. 
257.     # Prevent copying the destination into itself
258.     if _is_relative_to(src, dst_root):
259.         raise ValueError(f"Refusing to copy {src} into its own destination {dst_root}")
260. 
261.     def _should_ignore(name: str) -> bool:
262.         return name in ignore_names
263. 
264.     if src.is_dir():
265.         for item in src.iterdir():
266.             if _should_ignore(item.name):
267.                 continue
268.             target = dst_root / item.name
269.             if item.is_dir():
270.                 shutil.copytree(item, target, dirs_exist_ok=True, symlinks=True)
271.             else:
272.                 target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
273.                 shutil.copy2(item, target)
274.     else:
275.         target = dst_root / src.name
276.         target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
277.         shutil.copy2(src, target)
278. 
279.     print(f"Persisted {src} -> {dst_root}")
280.     return dst_root

302. def dict_merge_shallow(old: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], new: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
303.     """
304.     Merge two dicts shallowly (one level).
305.     - If both old and new are None, return {}.
306.     - If only one is non-empty, return that one.
307.     - If both exist, new keys override old.
308.     """
309.     if old is None and new is None:
310.         return {}
311.     if old is None:
312.         return dict(new)
313.     if new is None:
314.         return dict(old)
315.     return {**old, **new}

331. def is_1d_vector(x: object) -> TypeGuard[Array1D]:
332.     """
333.     Return True if x is a 1-D numeric-like sequence:
334.      - pandas.Series,
335.      - numpy.ndarray with ndim == 1,
336.      - list/tuple of scalars convertible to a 1-D array.
337.     """
338.     try:
339.         if isinstance(x, (str, bytes)):
340.             return False
341.         if isinstance(x, pd.Series):
342.             return True
343.         if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
344.             return x.ndim == 1
345.         if is_list_like(x):
346.             try:
347.                 arr = np.asarray(x)
348.             except Exception:
349.                 return False
350.             return arr.ndim == 1
351.         if isinstance(x, Sequence):
352.             try:
353.                 arr = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
354.             except (ValueError, TypeError):
355.                 return False
356.             return arr.ndim == 1
357.         return False
358.     except Exception as e:
359.         raise e

<sub>⏱️ 74m 4s</sub>

### 💭 Reasoning

*70 tests passed, 20 failed. All failures are in `test_registry.py`. The issue is that `register_dataframe` returns `None` when it shouldn't. Let me investigate this more. Let me look at what's happening. The `register_dataframe` function requires either a df or a raw_path to be valid. When we call `registry.register_dataframe(sample_df, "test_id")` without a raw_path, it tries to write the df to `WORKING_DIRECTORY / f"{df_id}.csv"`. But the test uses the `registry` fixture which is a fresh `DataFrameRegistry(capacity=5)` created in conftest.py.


When raw_path is empty, the function constructs a path and attempts to write the dataframe to that location, but if the write operation fails, it returns `None` instead of the expected result.

Actually, I'm noticing a potential bug here — `path` gets set from the empty raw_path before it's updated to point to the working directory, so the normalized path might be resolving to the current working directory instead of the intended location. Let me trace through the actual function to confirm the order of operations. I see the issue now—when `raw_path` is empty, `path` gets computed as the current working directory before `raw_path` is reassigned to the generated CSV file path, so `_write_df` ends up trying to write the DataFrame directly to the cwd instead of a file. This is a bug in the DataFrameRegistry where the path normalization happens too early, and the fix would need to either recompute `path` after updating `raw_path` or defer the path computation until after `raw_path` is properly set.

Looking at the test stub in test_intelligent_data_detective.py, it appears to have the same logic flow with the same vulnerability.

The issue is clear now: when `raw_path` is empty, it gets set to a resolved path string, but `path` still references the original empty string which resolves to the current directory. Since the current directory exists as a directory (not a file), the condition `(not path.exists() or not path.is_file())` evaluates to true, causing `_write_df` to be called with a directory path instead of a file path, which fails. The solution is to recalculate `path` after updating `raw_path` so they stay in sync.*

def _resolve_artifact_path(
        file_name: str,
        *,
        config: Optional[RunnableConfig],
        subdir: Optional[str] = None,
        create_parents: bool = True,
    ) -> PathlibPath:
        """Resolve file_name relative to (or validated within) the artifacts dir."""
        if not file_name or not isinstance(file_name, str):
            raise ValueError("file_name must be a non-empty string.")        base = _get_artifacts_base(config)
        if subdir:
            base = (base / subdir).resolve()        base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)        candidate = PathlibPath(file_name)
        path = (base / candidate).resolve() if not candidate.is_absolute() else candidate.resolve()        if not _is_subpath(path, base):
            raise ValueError(f"Refusing to access path outside artifacts root: {path}")

        if create_parents:
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        return path

class MyChatOpenai(ChatOpenAI):        def _get_request_payload_mod(
            self,
            input_: LanguageModelInput,
            *,
            stop: Optional[list[str]] = None,
            **kwargs: Any,
        ) -> dict:
            messages = self._convert_input(input_).to_messages()
            if stop is not None:
                kwargs["stop"] = stop            payload = {**self._default_params, **kwargs}            if self._use_responses_api(payload):
                if self.use_previous_response_id:
                    last_messages, previous_response_id = _get_last_messages(messages)
                    payload_to_use = last_messages if previous_response_id else messages
                    if previous_response_id:
                        payload["previous_response_id"] = previous_response_id
                    payload = _construct_responses_api_payload(payload_to_use, payload)
                else:
                    payload = _construct_responses_api_payload(messages, payload)
            else:
                payload["messages"] = [_convert_message_to_dict(m) for m in messages]
            return payload        def _get_request_payload(
            self,
            input_: LanguageModelInput,
            *,
            stop: Optional[list[str]] = None,
            **kwargs: Any,
        ) -> dict:
            payload = self._get_request_payload_mod(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)
            if "max_tokens" in payload:
                payload["max_completion_tokens"] = payload.pop("max_tokens")            if self.model_name and re.match(r"^o\d", self.model_name):
                for message in payload.get("messages", []):
                    if message["role"] == "system":
                        message["role"] = "developer"
            return payload

def _get_artifacts_base(config: Optional[RunnableConfig]) -> PathlibPath:
        """Resolve the base directory for artifacts."""
        try:
            cfg = getattr(config, "configurable", None) or {}
            runtime = cfg.get("runtime")
            if runtime is not None and getattr(runtime, "artifacts_dir", None):
                base = PathlibPath(runtime.artifacts_dir)
                base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                return base
        except Exception:

                base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        except Exception:

````
1. # Supervisor-Subagent Pattern
2. 
3. The supervisor-subagent pattern uses a central coordinator (supervisor) to analyze tasks and delegate work to specialized subagents. This is a common multi-agent pattern for complex workflows.
4. 
5. ## When to Use
6. 
7. Use supervisor-subagent when:
8. - You have multiple specialized agents with distinct capabilities
9. - Tasks require dynamic routing based on context
10. - You need centralized coordination and decision-making
11. - Subagents need to communicate through a central authority
12. 
13. ## Architecture
14. 
15. ```
16. User Request → Supervisor → Subagent 1
17.                 ↓            ↓
18.               Subagent 2     Back to Supervisor
19.                 ↓            ↓
20.               Subagent 3     Decision (continue/finish)
21. ```
22. 
23. ## Core Components
24. 
25. ### 1. State Schema
26. 
27. The state must support message accumulation and routing decisions:
28. 
29. **Python:**
30. ```python
31. from typing import TypedDict, Literal, Annotated
32. from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
33. from langchain_core.messages import BaseMessage
34. 
35. class SupervisorState(TypedDict):
36.     """State for supervisor pattern.
37. 
38.     Attributes:
39.         messages: Chat history with add_messages reducer
40.         next: Next agent to route to
41.         current_agent: Currently active agent
42.         task_complete: Whether the task is complete
43.     """
44.     messages: Annotated[list[BaseMessage], add_messages]
45.     next: Literal["researcher", "writer", "reviewer", "FINISH"]
46.     current_agent: str
47.     task_complete: bool
48. ```
49. 
50. **JavaScript:**
51. ```typescript
52. import { BaseMessage } from "@langchain/core/messages";
53. import { Annotation } from "@langchain/langgraph";
54. 
55. export const SupervisorStateAnnotation = Annotation.Root({
56.   messages: Annotation<BaseMessage[]>({
57.     reducer: (left, right) => left.concat(right),
58.     default: () => [],
59.   }),
60.   next: Annotation<"researcher" | "writer" | "reviewer" | "FINISH">({
61.     reducer: (_, right) => right,
62.   }),
63.   currentAgent: Annotation<string>({
64.     reducer: (_, right) => right,
65.   }),
66.   taskComplete: Annotation<boolean>({
67.     reducer: (_, right) => right,
68.     default: () => false,
69.   }),
70. });
71. ```
72. 
73. **Key features:**
74. - `messages`: Accumulates conversation history with `add_messages` reducer
75. - `next`: Stores routing decision (which agent or FINISH)
76. - `current_agent`: Tracks which agent last acted
77. - `task_complete`: Boolean flag for termination
78. 
79. ### 2. Supervisor Node
80. 
81. The supervisor analyzes the current state and decides which subagent should act next:
82. 
83. **Python:**
84. ```python
85. from langchain_core.messages import SystemMessage
86. from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate, MessagesPlaceholder
87. from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
88. 
89. model = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4")
90. 
91. SUPERVISOR_PROMPT = """You are a supervisor managing a team of agents.
92. 
93. Available agents:
94. - researcher: Searches for information and gathers facts
95. - writer: Creates written content based on research
96. - reviewer: Reviews and improves written content
97. 
98. Analyze the conversation and decide which agent should act next.
99. If the task is complete, respond with "FINISH".
100. 
101. Consider:
102. 1. What has been accomplished so far
103. 2. What still needs to be done
104. 3. Which agent is best suited for the next step
105. """
106. 
107. def supervisor_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
108.     """Supervisor decides which agent acts next."""
109.     messages = state["messages"]
110. 
111.     prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
112.         ("system", SUPERVISOR_PROMPT),
113.         MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name="messages"),
114.         ("system", "Who should act next? Respond with: researcher, writer, reviewer, or FINISH")
115.     ])
116. 
117.     chain = prompt | model
118.     response = chain.invoke({"messages": messages})
119. 
120.     # Extract routing decision from LLM response
121.     next_agent = response.content.strip()
122. 
123.     # Validate routing decision
124.     valid_options = ["researcher", "writer", "reviewer", "FINISH"]
125.     if next_agent not in valid_options:
126.         next_agent = "FINISH"  # Default to finish if invalid
127. 
128.     return {
129.         "next": next_agent,
130.         "current_agent": "supervisor"
131.     }
132. ```
133. 
134. **JavaScript:**
135. ```typescript
136. import { ChatOpenAI } from "@langchain/openai";
137. import { ChatPromptTemplate, MessagesPlaceholder } from "@langchain/core/prompts";
138. 
139. const model = new ChatOpenAI({ model: "gpt-4" });
140. 
141. const SUPERVISOR_PROMPT = `You are a supervisor managing a team of agents.
142. 
143. Available agents:
144. - researcher: Searches for information and gathers facts
145. - writer: Creates written content based on research
146. - reviewer: Reviews and improves written content
147. 
148. Analyze the conversation and decide which agent should act next.
149. If the task is complete, respond with "FINISH".`;
150. 
151. export async function supervisorNode(state: any): Promise<Partial<any>> {
152.   const messages = state.messages;
153. 
154.   const prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.fromMessages([
155.     ["system", SUPERVISOR_PROMPT],
156.     new MessagesPlaceholder("messages"),
157.     ["system", "Who should act next? Respond with: researcher, writer, reviewer, or FINISH"]
158.   ]);
159. 
160.   const chain = prompt.pipe(model);
161.   const response = await chain.invoke({ messages });
162. 
163.   let nextAgent = response.content.trim();
164. 
165.   // Validate routing decision
166.   const validOptions = ["researcher", "writer", "reviewer", "FINISH"];
167.   if (!validOptions.includes(nextAgent)) {
168.     nextAgent = "FINISH";
169.   }
170. 
171.   return {
172.     next: nextAgent,
173.     currentAgent: "supervisor"
174.   };
175. }
176. ```
177. 
178. **Key implementation details:**
179. - Uses LLM to make routing decisions based on context
180. - Validates routing decision against valid options
181. - Defaults to FINISH for invalid routes
182. - Can be enhanced with structured output for more reliable routing
183. 
184. ### 3. Subagent Nodes
185. 
186. Each subagent is a specialized node that performs specific tasks:
187. 
188. **Python:**
189. ```python
190. from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage
191. from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate, MessagesPlaceholder
192. from langchain_community.tools.tavily_search import TavilySearchResults
193. 
194. # Research agent with search tool
195. search_tool = TavilySearchResults(max_results=3)
196. 
197. def researcher_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
198.     """Research agent searches for information."""
199.     messages = state["messages"]
200. 
201.     # Get the latest user query
202.     latest_query = messages[-1].content
203. 
204.     # Perform search
205.     search_results = search_tool.invoke(latest_query)
206. 
207.     # Format results
208.     result_text = "Research findings:\n"
209.     for i, result in enumerate(search_results, 1):
210.         result_text += f"\n{i}. {result['content']}\n"
211. 
212.     return {
213.         "messages": [HumanMessage(content=result_text)],
214.         "current_agent": "researcher"
215.     }
216. 
217. 
218. # Reuse the same model defined in the supervisor section
219. def writer_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
220.     """Writer creates content based on research."""
221.     messages = state["messages"]
222. 
223.     prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
224.         ("system", "You are a skilled writer. Create well-written content based on the research provided."),
225.         MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name="messages"),
226.         ("system", "Write your content now:")
227.     ])
228. 
229.     chain = prompt | model
230.     response = chain.invoke({"messages": messages})
231. 
232.     return {
233.         "messages": [HumanMessage(content=response.content)],
234.         "current_agent": "writer"
235.     }
236. 
237. 
238. def reviewer_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
239.     """Reviewer checks and improves content."""
240.     messages = state["messages"]
241. 
242.     prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
243.         ("system", "You are an editor. Review the content and suggest improvements."),

246.     ])
247. 
248.     chain = prompt | model

250.

262. 
263. const searchTool = new TavilySearchResults({ maxResults: 3 });

265. export async function researcherNode(state: any): Promise<Partial<any>> {
266.   const messages = state.messages;

274.   });

279.   };
280. }
281. 
282. export async function writerNode(state: any): Promise<Partial<any>> {
283.   const messages = state.messages;
284. 
285.   const prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.fromMessages([
286.     ["system", "You are a skilled writer. Create well-written content based on the research provided."],
287.     new MessagesPlaceholder("messages"),
288.     ["system", "Write your content now:"]
289.   ]);
290.

297.   };
298. }

300. 
301. ### 4. Graph Assembly
302. 
303. Wire together supervisor and subagents with proper routing:
304. 
305. **Python:**
306. ```python
307. from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
308. 
309. def create_supervisor_graph() -> StateGraph:
310.     """Assemble supervisor-subagent graph."""
311.     graph = StateGraph(SupervisorState)
312. 
313.     # Add nodes
314.     graph.add_node("supervisor", supervisor_node)
315.     graph.add_node("researcher", researcher_node)
316.     graph.add_node("writer", writer_node)
317.     graph.add_node("reviewer", reviewer_node)
318. 
319.     # Set entry point
320.     graph.set_entry_point("supervisor")
321. 
322.     # Add conditional edges from supervisor
323.     graph.add_conditional_edges(
324.         "supervisor",
325.         lambda state: state["next"],
326.         {
327.             "researcher": "researcher",
328.             "writer": "writer",
329.             "reviewer": "reviewer",
330.             "FINISH": END
331.         }
332.     )
333. 
334.     # All subagents route back to supervisor
335.     graph.add_edge("researcher", "supervisor")
336.     graph.add_edge("writer", "supervisor")
337.     graph.add_edge("reviewer", "supervisor")
338. 
339.     return graph.compile()
340. ```
341. 
342. **JavaScript:**
343. ```typescript
344. import { StateGraph, START, END } from "@langchain/langgraph";
345. 
346. export function createSupervisorGraph() {
347.   const graph = new StateGraph(SupervisorStateAnnotation)
348.     .addNode("supervisor", supervisorNode)
349.     .addNode("researcher", researcherNode)
350.     .addNode("writer", writerNode)
351.     .addNode("reviewer", reviewerNode)
352. 
353.     .addEdge(START, "supervisor")
354. 
355.     .addConditionalEdges(
356.       "supervisor",
357.       (state) => state.next,
358.       {
359.         researcher: "researcher",
360.         writer: "writer",
361.         reviewer: "reviewer",
362.         FINISH: END
363.       }
364.     )
365. 
366.     .addEdge("researcher", "supervisor")
367.     .addEdge("writer", "supervisor")
368.     .addEdge("reviewer", "supervisor");
369. 
370.   return graph.compile();
371. }
372. ```
373. 
374. ## Best Practices
375. 
376. ### 1. Clear Agent Responsibilities
377. 
378. Define clear, non-overlapping responsibilities for each subagent:
379. 
380. ```python
381. SUPERVISOR_PROMPT = """Available agents and their capabilities:
382. 
383. - researcher:
384.   * Searches web for current information
385.   * Gathers facts, statistics, citations
386.   * Provides source references
387. 
388. - writer:
389.   * Creates articles, blog posts, documentation
390.   * Organizes information coherently
391.   * Applies appropriate tone and style
392. 
393. - reviewer:
394.   * Checks factual accuracy
395.   * Improves clarity and grammar
396.   * Ensures consistency with requirements
397. """
398. ```
399. 
400. ### 2. Structured Routing
401. 
402. Use structured output for more reliable routing:
403. 
404. ```python
405. from pydantic import BaseModel
406. from typing import Literal
407. 
408. class RouteDecision(BaseModel):
409.     """Structured routing decision."""
410.     next_agent: Literal["researcher", "writer", "reviewer", "FINISH"]
411.     reasoning: str
412. 
413. def supervisor_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
414.     """Supervisor with structured output."""
415.     messages = state["messages"]
416. 
417.     # Use structured output for routing
418.     structured_model = model.with_structured_output(RouteDecision)
419. 
420.     decision = structured_model.invoke([
421.         SystemMessage(content=SUPERVISOR_PROMPT),
422.         *messages,
423.         SystemMessage(content="Decide which agent should act next.")
424.     ])
425. 
426.     return {
427.         "next": decision.next_agent,
428.         "current_agent": "supervisor"
429.     }
430. ```
431. 
432. ### 3. Loop Prevention
433. 
434. Add loop detection to prevent infinite cycles:
435. 
436. ```python
437. def supervisor_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
438.     """Supervisor with loop detection."""
439.     messages = state["messages"]
440. 
441.     # Check for repeated patterns
442.     recent_agents = [
443.         msg.name for msg in messages[-6:]
444.         if hasattr(msg, 'name')
445.     ]
446. 
447.     # If same agent called 3+ times in a row, force different route
448.     if len(recent_agents) >= 3 and len(set(recent_agents[-3:])) == 1:
449.         return {
450.             "next": "FINISH",
451.             "current_agent": "supervisor",
452.             "messages": [SystemMessage(content="Detected loop, completing task.")]
453.         }
454. 
455.     # Normal routing logic...
456. ```
457. 
458. ### 4. Context Management
459. 
460. Keep context size manageable by summarizing history:
461. 
462. ```python
463. def supervisor_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
464.     """Supervisor with context summarization."""
465.     messages = state["messages"]
466. 
467.     # If context gets too long, summarize older messages
468.     if len(messages) > 20:
469.         # Summarize first N messages
470.         summary_prompt = f"Summarize these messages concisely: {messages[:10]}"
471.         summary = model.invoke(summary_prompt).content
472. 
473.         # Keep recent messages + summary
474.         messages = [
475.             SystemMessage(content=f"Previous context: {summary}"),
476.             *messages[10:]
477.         ]
478. 
479.     # Continue with routing...
480. ```
481. 
482. ## Common Variations
483. 
484. ### Parallel Execution
485. 
486. Execute multiple subagents in parallel:
487. 
488. ```python
489. from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
490. 
491. def create_parallel_supervisor_graph():
492.     """Supervisor that can dispatch multiple agents in parallel."""
493.     graph = StateGraph(SupervisorState)
494. 
495.     graph.add_node("supervisor", supervisor_node)
496.     graph.add_node("researcher", researcher_node)
497.     graph.add_node("fact_checker", fact_checker_node)
498. 
499.     # Both can run in parallel
500.     graph.add_edge("supervisor", "researcher")
501.     graph.add_edge("supervisor", "fact_checker")
502. 
503.     # Use Send for parallel execution
504.     # (Requires modified state to track parallel results)
505. 
506.     return graph.compile()
507. ```
508. 
509. ### Hierarchical Supervision
510. 
511. Nest supervisors for complex workflows:
512. 
513. ```python
514. # Top-level supervisor
515. def top_supervisor_node(state):
516.     """Delegates to sub-supervisors."""
517.     # Route to research_team or writing_team
518.     pass
519. 
520. # Research team supervisor
521. def research_supervisor_node(state):
522.     """Manages research subagents."""
523.     # Route to web_searcher, document_reader, etc.
524.     pass
525. ```
526. 
527. ## Debugging Tips
528. 
529. ### 1. Trace Agent Decisions
530. 
531. Log supervisor routing decisions:
532. 
533. ```python
534. def supervisor_node(state: SupervisorState) -> dict:
535.     """Supervisor with decision logging."""
536.     decision = get_routing_decision(state)
537. 
538.     print(f"Supervisor decision: {decision}")
539.     print(f"Current state: {len(state['messages'])} messages")
540. 
541.     return {"next": decision, "current_agent": "supervisor"}
542. ```
543. 
544. ### 2. Visualize Flow
545. 
546. Use LangSmith tracing to visualize the agent flow:
547. 
548. ```python
549. import os
550. os.environ["LANGSMITH_TRACING"] = "true"
551. os.environ["LANGSMITH_API_KEY"] = "<your-api-key>"
552. 
553. result = graph.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="Research AI")]})
554. ```
555. 
556. ### 3. Test Routing Logic
557. 
558. Unit test supervisor routing decisions:
559. 
560. ```python
561. def test_supervisor_routing():
562.     """Test supervisor routes correctly."""
563.     # Test state with research needed
564.     state = {
565.         "messages": [HumanMessage(content="Tell me about AI")],
566.         "next": "",
567.         "current_agent": "",
568.         "task_complete": False
569.     }
570. 
571.     result = supervisor_node(state)
572.     assert result["next"] == "researcher"
573. 
574.     # Test state with writing needed
575.     state["messages"].append(HumanMessage(content="Research results: ..."))
576.     result = supervisor_node(state)
577.     assert result["next"] == "writer"
578. ```
579. 
580. ## Performance Considerations
581. 
582. ### Token Usage
583. 
584. Supervisor patterns use more tokens due to:
585. - LLM calls for routing decisions
586. - Full context passed to supervisor each iteration
587. - Message accumulation over time
588. 
589. Mitigation strategies:
590. - Use cheaper models for routing (e.g., GPT-4o-mini)
591. - Summarize context when it grows large
592. - Cache supervisor prompts
593. - Use structured output to reduce parsing
594. 
595. ### Latency
596. 
597. Sequential routing adds latency:
598. - Each supervisor decision requires an LLM call
599. - Subagents wait for supervisor decisions
600. - No parallel execution by default
601. 
602. Optimizations:
603. - Use faster models for supervisor
604. - Implement parallel execution where possible
605. - Cache common routing patterns
606. - Consider router pattern for simpler routing
607. 
608. ## Migration Path
609. 
610. Converting a simple agent to supervisor pattern:
611. 
612. **Before (simple agent):**
613. ```python
614. def agent(state):
615.     # Do research
616.     # Do writing
617.     # Do review
618.     return result
619. ```
620. 
621. **After (supervisor pattern):**
622. ```python
623. # Split into specialized nodes
624. def researcher(state): ...
625. def writer(state): ...
626. def reviewer(state): ...
627. 
628. # Add supervisor for coordination
629. def supervisor(state):
630.     # Decide which specialized agent to call
631.     return routing_decision
632. 
633. # Assemble graph
634. graph = create_supervisor_graph()
635. ```
636. 
637. ## When Not to Use
638. 
639. Avoid supervisor pattern when:
640. - **Simple sequential flow**: Use basic graph edges instead
641. - **Deterministic routing**: Use router pattern instead
642. - **No coordination needed**: Use parallel execution
643. - **High latency sensitivity**: Consider simpler patterns
644. 
645. ## Additional Resources
646. 
647. - Multi-Agent Tutorials (Python): https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/multi-agent/subagents-personal-assistant
648. - Multi-Agent Tutorials (JavaScript): https://docs.langchain.com/oss/javascript/langchain/multi-agent/subagents-personal-assistant
649. - LangGraph Graph API: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/graph-api
650. - State Management Guide: See state-management-patterns.md
651.
````

def handle_tool_errors(func):
    """Decorator for consistent error handling across tool functions."""
    @functools.wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        try:
            df_id = None            if args and isinstance(args[0], str):
                df_id = args[0]
            elif 'df_id' in kwargs:
                df_id = kwargs['df_id']
            elif args and hasattr(args[0], 'df_id'):
                df_id = args[0].df_id            if df_id and not validate_dataframe_exists(df_id):=== validate_dataframe_exists ===
def validate_dataframe_exists(df_id: str) -> bool:
    """Validates the existence and validity of a dataframe by its ID."""
    if not df_id or not isinstance(df_id, str):
        return False    try:
        df = global_df_registry.get_dataframe(df_id)
        if df is not None:
            return not df.empty        raw_path = global_df_registry.get_raw_path_from_id(df_id)
        if raw_path and os.path.exists(raw_path):
            try:
                df = pd.read_csv(raw_path)
                if df is not None and not df.empty:=== DataFrameRegistryError ===
class DataFrameRegistryError(Exception):

    def __init__(self, message):
        self.message = message
        super().__init__(self.message)    def __str__(self): return self.message
    def __repr__(self): return self.message
    def to_dict(self): return {"error": self.message}=== ProgressReport ===

1153. def handle_tool_errors(func):

1155.     @functools.wraps(func)
1156.     def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
1157.         try:
1158.             df_id = None
1159. 
1160.             if args and isinstance(args[0], str):
1161.                 df_id = args[0]
1162.             elif 'df_id' in kwargs:
1163.                 df_id = kwargs['df_id']
1164.             elif args and hasattr(args[0], 'df_id'):
1165.                 df_id = args[0].df_id
1166. 
1167.             if df_id and not validate_dataframe_exists(df_id):
1168.                 error_msg = f"Error: DataFrame with ID '{df_id}' not found or is invalid."
1169.                 logging.error(f'{func.__name__}: {error_msg}')

1171.

1173.

1181.             logging.error(f"{func.__name__}: {error_msg}")

13. # Notebook Specialist
14. 
15. You are the specialist for `IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb`, the single-file source of truth for the entire IDD system. All 7 LangGraph agents, the State TypedDict, tools, and graph wiring live inside this notebook's 27 cells. Read `.github/instructions/notebook.instructions.md` before every edit.
16. 
17. ## Cell map (authoritative)
18. | Cell | Role |
19. |------|------|
20. | 1 | Environment setup, API key handling, package install |
21. | 4 | Core imports and type aliases |
22. | 5 | `MyChatOpenai` – custom ChatOpenAI subclass |
23. | 7 | Pydantic models (`BaseNoExtrasModel`, `State`, `AnalysisConfig`, …) |
24. | 8 | `DataFrameRegistry` – thread-safe LRU DataFrame manager |
25. | 10 | Agent prompt templates and `DEFAULT_TOOLING_GUIDELINES` |
26. | 12/13 | All tools (~78 functions) + `@handle_tool_errors` decorator |
27. | 14+ | Agent construction, LangGraph graph wiring, graph compilation |
28. 
29. ## Hard rules
30. - **Never delete cells.** Append new cells; never renumber or reorder existing ones.
31. - **Use `MyChatOpenai` everywhere** in the notebook — never raw `ChatOpenAI`.
32. - **All agent output models must extend `BaseNoExtrasModel`** and include `reply_msg_to_supervisor`, `finished_this_task`, and `expect_reply` fields.
33. - **State fields with reducers (`Annotated[..., keep_first]`, `Annotated[..., operator.add]`, etc.) must never be assigned directly** — state merges will silently break.
34. - **Every new tool must use `@handle_tool_errors` and call `validate_dataframe_exists(df_id)` first** when it touches a DataFrame.
35. - **Register new tools** in the appropriate list (`data_cleaning_tools`, `analyst_tools`, etc.) at the point of definition inside Cell 13.
36. - **All file writes go through `_resolve_artifact_path()`** — never bypass with `open()`.
37. - **Memory namespaces** are `('memories', '<kind>')` where kind ∈ `{conversation, analysis, cleaning, visualization, insights, errors}`. TTL and per-kind limits come from `memory_config.yaml`, not hardcode them.
38. 
39. ## Focus paths
40. - `IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb`
41. - `memory_config.yaml`
42. 
43. ## Validation after notebook edits
44. ```bash
45. # Confirm cells load without syntax error
46. python3 -c "import json; cells=json.load(open('IntelligentDataDetective_beta_v5.ipynb'))['cells']; print(f'{len(cells)} cells OK')"
47. # Run unit tests (no API keys required)
48. python3 -m pytest test_intelligent_data_detective.py -v
49. ```

### 💬 Copilot

Here’s the critical feedback I’d give.

## Biggest issues

- **Blocking: `langgraph-validator` is over-promising.**  
  Your plan says it will validate reducer/type consistency against the **State schema**, but `idd_core` explicitly excludes `State` (`idd_core.py:1027-1030`). Unless this agent reads the production notebook/script as its source of truth, it cannot do the audit you describe.

- **Blocking: several proposed tests assert behavior the code does not enforce.**
  - `FileResult.category_tag` is just `str`, not a `Literal` (`idd_core.py:536-545`).
  - `VizFeedback.redo_list` has no conditional validator tied to `grade` (`idd_core.py:760-763`).
  - `DataVisualization.visualization_id` uniqueness is only described, not enforced (`idd_core.py:498-505`).
  These tests will either fail incorrectly or force product behavior changes that weren’t in the plan.

- **Important: you’re mixing two different routing/type domains.**
  - `AgentMembers.agent_type` has 9 values (`idd_core.py:174-180`)
  - `AgentId` / `AgentOrSupervisor` includes internal nodes like `viz_worker`, `viz_join`, `FINISH`, `END` (`idd_core.py:215-223`)
  Some test ideas blur those together. That’s a recipe for false positives.

## Scope / design concerns

- **Agent ownership overlaps with existing agents.**  
  `idd-test-specialist` overlaps heavily with `backend-python-specialist`, which already owns Python/test changes and is the notebook specialist’s delegate for test-file edits (`.github/agents/backend-python-specialist.agent.md`, `.github/agents/notebook-specialist.agent.md`).  
  If you add the new agent, also update existing agent docs or you’ll create ambiguous ownership.

- **`idd-pipeline-debugger` and `langgraph-validator` overlap.**  
  Both touch routing stalls / topology / reducer conflicts. I’d separate them more clearly:
  - debugger = runtime diagnosis + repro cases
  - validator = static topology/schema checks only

- **`test_pipeline_stages.py` sounds more like component/unit than integration** unless it imports the real notebook `State` or exercises actual graph nodes. If it only simulates reducer merges, it overlaps with `test_reducers.py` and `test_state_flow.py`.

- **`dict_merge_shallow` “thread safety” is not a meaningful test target.**  
  It’s a pure function. Thread-safety belongs on `DataFrameRegistry`, which you already test.

## Answers to your 7 questions

1. **`VizFeedback` empty `redo_list` check?**  
   Not enforced by the model. It’s convention only, unless you add a validator.

2. **`FileResult.category_tag` restricted?**  
   No. It is currently plain `str`, despite the description listing 4 options.

3. **Should `agent_list_default_generator` be tested?**  
   **Maybe, but only if it is actually used.** It currently returns 7 agents and omits `report_orchestrator` and `report_section_worker` (`idd_core.py:203-212`). That could be intentional or a bug. Worth testing only if callers rely on it.

4. **Missing valuable edge cases?**
   - `validate_dataframe_exists` raw-path fallback + re-registration path
   - empty-but-existing CSV vs missing CSV
   - `handle_tool_errors` exception mapping for `FileNotFoundError`, `KeyError`, `EmptyDataError`, `ParserError`
   - `CLASS_TO_AGENT` mapping consistency (`idd_core.py:1046-1058`)
   - mismatch between `AgentMembers`, `AgentId`, and `SendAgentMessage.recipient`

5. **Are the 3 agents well scoped?**  
   **Not yet.** Main problem is overlap with existing repo agents and overlap between debugger/validator.

6. **Should `test_pipeline_stages.py` be unit or integration?**  
   **Unit/component** if it only simulates merges/models.  
   **Integration** only if it uses the real notebook `State`, node functions, or compiled graph behavior.

7. **Is `add_messages` dedup test fragile?**  
   **Yes.** Since `add_messages` comes from LangGraph, exact dedup semantics may vary by version. Test only behavior you own, or pin the version and document that dependency.

## Recommended adjustments

- Narrow `langgraph-validator` to **notebook-backed validation** only.
- Remove tests for unenforced invariants unless you also plan product changes.
- Split routing tests into:
  - `AgentMembers` model validity
  - `SendAgentMessage.recipient` / `AgentOrSupervisor` validity
  - graph/node routing invariants
- Put reducer-simulation tests in unit/component, not integration.
- Update existing agent docs if you introduce new specialists; otherwise they’ll conflict.

Overall: **good direction, but the current plan overstates what the sanitized module can validate and includes several tests for behavior that doesn’t exist yet.**

### 💭 Reasoning

*The rubber duck critique is very helpful. Key findings I should adopt:

1. **`langgraph-validator` needs to read production notebook/script** (not just idd_core) for State schema validation — or scope it down to static topology checks from the compiled graph
2. **Remove tests for unenforced invariants**: `FileResult.category_tag` is `str`, `VizFeedback.redo_list` has no conditional validator, `DataVisualization.visualization_id` uniqueness not enforced
3. **Separate routing domains**: AgentMembers.agent_type (9 values) vs AgentOrSupervisor (includes viz_worker, viz_join, FINISH, END) — these are different


4. **idd-test-specialist and backend-python-specialist have overlapping scope** — I need to clarify who owns what or consolidate them
5. **idd-pipeline-debugger and langgraph-validator are doing similar work** — I should draw clearer boundaries between them
6. **test_pipeline_stages.py is really a unit test** since it only exercises models and reducers, not integration behavior
7. **The add_messages dedup test is too brittle** — I should only test the behavior I actually control

Now I'm planning the revised approach. For the agents, I'm thinking about three new ones but with much tighter scoping, starting with clarifying what idd-test-specialist actually owns versus what backend-python-specialist handles.

The idd-test-specialist will focus on test harness work and own the tests directory, idd_core.py, and pytest configuration, while explicitly staying out of production code like the notebook and memory_enhancements.py.

The idd-pipeline-debugger will have read-only access to the production script for runtime diagnosis — tracing state transitions and identifying stalls — but won't do topology validation.

The langgraph-validator will be purely static, reading the production notebook directly to validate the graph structure, nodes, edges, and routing types using the validation utility.

Now I'm planning out the test suite with about 30 unit tests covering the pipeline models — checking edge cases like empty fields, forbidden extra fields, Literal type enforcement, and consistency rules across CleaningMetadata, AnalysisInsights, VizSpec, VizFeedback, DataVisualization, VisualizationResults, and ReportOutline.

Then I need around 15 tests for agent messages, validating SendAgentMessage flags in both emergency and normal paths, ensuring recipients are valid AgentOrSupervisor types, testing MessagesToAgentsList with various list sizes, and confirming all 9 known agent types pass validation while unknown types raise errors.

For the tool errors tests, I'm covering handle_tool_errors with different df_id argument patterns, validate_dataframe_exists across registered/unregistered/empty/None cases, the raw-path fallback when dataframes are evicted from memory, error representations, and ensuring decorated functions return error messages rather than exceptions when encountering unregistered IDs or file/key errors. I should also verify CLASS_TO_AGENT mapping stays consistent, then merge the class_to_agent tests into the agent_messages file rather than keeping them separate.

For the pipeline stages tests, I'm reconsidering whether to keep them as integration—they should focus on multi-step state merge patterns rather than just reducer behavior, while pure reducer logic moves to unit tests. The supervisor loop tests will validate message accumulation over multiple rounds, the merge_int_sum counter incrementing through iterations, all nine AgentMembers routing types, the distinction between Routing and AgentOrSupervisor, and that the final state remains consistent after multiple reducer cycles.

100. def dict_merge_shallow(old: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], new: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
101.     """Merge two dicts shallowly (one level)."""
102.     if old is None and new is None:
103.         return {}
104.     if old is None:
105.         return dict(new)
106.     if new is None:
107.         return dict(old)
108.     return {**old, **new}

123.     """Return True if x is a 1-D numeric-like sequence."""
124.     try:
125.         if isinstance(x, (str, bytes)):
126.             return False
127.         if isinstance(x, pd.Series):

139.                 arr = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
140.             except (ValueError, TypeError):

142.             return arr.ndim == 1
143.         return False

341.     class MyChatOpenai(ChatOpenAI):
342. 
343.         def _get_request_payload_mod(
344.             self,
345.             input_: LanguageModelInput,
346.             *,
347.             stop: Optional[list[str]] = None,
348.             **kwargs: Any,
349.         ) -> dict:
350.             messages = self._convert_input(input_).to_messages()
351.             if stop is not None:
352.                 kwargs["stop"] = stop
353. 
354.             payload = {**self._default_params, **kwargs}
355. 
356.             if self._use_responses_api(payload):
357.                 if self.use_previous_response_id:
358.                     last_messages, previous_response_id = _get_last_messages(messages)
359.                     payload_to_use = last_messages if previous_response_id else messages
360.                     if previous_response_id:
361.                         payload["previous_response_id"] = previous_response_id
362.                     payload = _construct_responses_api_payload(payload_to_use, payload)
363.                 else:
364.                     payload = _construct_responses_api_payload(messages, payload)
365.             else:
366.                 payload["messages"] = [_convert_message_to_dict(m) for m in messages]
367.             return payload
368. 
369.         def _get_request_payload(
370.             self,
371.             input_: LanguageModelInput,
372.             *,
373.             stop: Optional[list[str]] = None,
374.             **kwargs: Any,
375.         ) -> dict:
376.             payload = self._get_request_payload_mod(input_, stop=stop, **kwargs)
377.             if "max_tokens" in payload:
378.                 payload["max_completion_tokens"] = payload.pop("max_tokens")
379. 
380.             if self.model_name and re.match(r"^o\d", self.model_name):

573. Triplet = Tuple[int, str, str]  # (step_number, step_name, step_description)

576. def _assert_sorted_completed_no_dups(steps: List["PlanStep"]) -> List["PlanStep"]:
577.     nums = [s.step_number for s in steps]
578.     if nums != sorted(nums):
579.         raise ValueError("completed_steps must be sorted ascending by step_number.")
580.     for s in steps:
581.         if s.is_step_complete is not True:
582.             raise ValueError("All completed_steps must have is_step_complete=True.")
583. 
584.     seen: set[Triplet] = set()
585.     seen_nums: set[int] = set()
586.     for s in steps:
587.         t = (s.step_number, s.step_name, s.step_description)
588.         if t in seen:
589.             raise ValueError(f"Duplicate completed step detected: {t}")
590.         if s.step_number in seen_nums:
591.             raise ValueError(f"Duplicate step_number {s.step_number} in completed_steps")
592.         seen.add(t)
593.         seen_nums.add(s.step_number)
594.     return steps

773. class DataFrameRegistry:
774.     def __init__(self, capacity=20):
775.         self._lock = threading.RLock()
776.         self.registry: Dict[str, dict] = {}
777.         self.df_id_to_raw_path: Dict[str, str] = {}
778.         self.cache = OrderedDict()
779.         self.capacity = capacity
780. 
781.     def _norm_path(self, p: str | PathlibPath) -> PathlibPath:
782.         return PathlibPath(p).expanduser().resolve() if isinstance(p, (str, PathlibPath)) else PathlibPath(p)
783. 
784.     def _write_df(self, df: pd.DataFrame, path: PathlibPath) -> bool:
785.         try:
786.             path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
787.             suf = path.suffix.lower()
788.             if suf == ".csv":
789.                 df.to_csv(path, index=False)
790.             elif suf == ".parquet":
791.                 df.to_parquet(path, index=False)
792.             elif suf == ".pkl":
793.                 df.to_pickle(path)
794.             elif suf == ".json":
795.                 df.to_json(path, orient="records")
796.             else:
797.                 df.to_csv(path, index=False)
798.             return True
799.         except Exception as e:
800.             print(f"Error writing DataFrame to {path}: {e}")
801.             return False
802. 
803.     def _read_df(self, path: PathlibPath) -> pd.DataFrame:
804.         suf = path.suffix.lower()
805.         if suf == ".csv":
806.             return pd.read_csv(path)
807.         if suf == ".parquet":
808.             return pd.read_parquet(path)
809.         if suf == ".pkl":
810.             return pd.read_pickle(path)
811.         if suf == ".json":
812.             return pd.read_json(path, orient="records")
813.         return pd.read_csv(path)
814. 
815.     def _touch_cache(self, df_id: str, df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
816.         self.cache[df_id] = df
817.         self.cache.move_to_end(df_id)
818.         if len(self.cache) > self.capacity:
819.             evicted_id, _ = self.cache.popitem(last=False)
820.             if evicted_id in self.registry:
821.                 self.registry[evicted_id]["df"] = None
822.

863.     def register_dataframe(self, df=None, df_id=None, raw_path=""):
